Okay, add Thursday night and use the Friday morning nonstop. Not before 8 a.m. if possible.

Friday April 25 around 9:15 a.m. is the best fit. It is late enough that you do not need a brutal hotel departure, but early enough to be back in Denver before the day disappears. I would plan to leave Franklin around 6:15 a.m., return the SUV around 7:15 to 7:30, and clear security with a cushion.
Book the compact SUV too. I need enough room for two cartons and the demo laptop case, but I do not want something oversized.

Compact SUV at BNA from Sunday evening to Friday morning is set as the target. Add a note for hatchback cargo space or cargo cover if available. It is the right balance for cartons, suitcase, and parking ease.
Shipment plan: first carton to hotel, second to Nashville site, or both hotel?

Send carton one to the hotel, arriving no later than Monday morning, because you control it for Franklin and Murfreesboro. Send carton two to the Nashville site only if the coordinator gives a named receiver; otherwise send it to the hotel too. Put your name, arrival date, reservation number, and hold for guest on the hotel label.

Final plan: fly DEN to BNA nonstop Sunday April 20 in the midafternoon, with a window seat requested; return BNA to DEN nonstop Friday April 25 around 9:15 a.m., also with a window request. If it is not there by late morning, use your carry-on handouts for calibration and treat Tuesday Murfreesboro as the first full workbook need.

messages.content: I’m pivoting from work travel to a family weekend. Can we rough out Denver to Norfolk/Virginia Beach for June 20-23? Picnic is Saturday afternoon and brunch Sunday morning. My spouse is coming, and I’m debating flying Friday versus adding Thursday night so we aren’t rushed.

Yes. For this pass I’d compare three things together: Friday arrival versus Thursday arrival, beach hotel versus relatives-area hotel, and whether the rental car cost changes the hotel decision. Are you targeting ORF, and are the relatives closer to Virginia Beach, Norfolk, or Chesapeake?

ORF unless Richmond is dramatically better. Relatives are mostly around Chesapeake, but we’d like some beach time. I’m okay with a connection, just not a two-stop mess or a layover that eats half the day.

The DEN-ORF flight shapes look like this: 1) Friday one-stop via Washington, leaving late morning and arriving around 5:15 p.m.; manageable connection, least hotel cost, but not much cushion. 2) Friday afternoon via Charlotte; nicer departure time, but the layover is long and arrival is close to 11 p.m. 3) Thursday late afternoon or early evening via Washington; arrival around 10:45-11:15 p.m., adds one hotel night, but Friday becomes relaxed. Monday has a clean midday one-stop return that gets you back to Denver early evening.
Can the Friday one-stop get us there before 5, or is that wishful thinking? And yes, please factor in window seats if we get to seat selection.

The best Friday version is only barely before or around 5 depending on the exact fare bucket. I would not treat it as protected time. It works if Friday has no family obligation and you just need to sleep before the picnic. If there’s any Friday dinner or airport delay, Thursday night is safer. The seat piece is easy to handle after you pick the itinerary; I’ll check for windows before ticketing.

Hotels are the other half. I want either a true oceanfront/boardwalk stay or something closer to family in Chesapeake. I’d like the guest rating to be at least around 4.0. Pool and fitness room matter; hot tub is nice but not a deal breaker. Balcony if we do oceanfront.

Shortlist: Oceanfront/boardwalk - Hyatt House or Hilton Garden Inn Virginia Beach Oceanfront type property, roughly 4.2-4.4 guest score, easy beach walk, pool and fitness room, balcony-request or oceanfront king categories, but no reliable hot tub and parking is extra. Chesapeake/Greenbrier - Hyatt Place or Staybridge type property, around 4.2-4.5, cheaper, free or easier parking, pool and fitness, closer to relatives, no beach feel. Airport/Norfolk - useful only for a late Thursday arrival, cheaper, fine for one night, not a weekend base.
If the flight lands after 10:30 Thursday, would you do airport hotel first and move Friday, or just go straight to the beach?

For two people on a short weekend, I’d lean one hotel if the oceanfront rate is tolerable. It avoids packing up Friday, storing bags, and waiting for a second check-in. A split stay can save maybe $80-$140 the first night, but it makes Friday more chore-heavy. If you want the balcony request to have any chance, staying all four nights at the same beach hotel is cleaner.
My spouse will hate the hotel move. Price the beach option versus Chesapeake for Thursday through Monday. And do we need a car?

Rough math: oceanfront Thursday-Monday is likely $1,250-$1,450 all-in before rental, depending on parking and taxes. Chesapeake is more like $750-$900 all-in. I’d rent a car either way: ORF to Virginia Beach and Chesapeake is spread out, rideshares add up, and family errands plus weather make a car useful. Parking cost is the main downside if you stay oceanfront.
That difference stings. Is there a compromise that still feels like a beach weekend?

Two compromises: airport or Chesapeake Thursday, then oceanfront Friday-Sunday nights, which saves some money but adds the hotel shuffle; or Chesapeake all four nights with a planned beach block Saturday morning or Sunday afternoon. Cheapest and easiest for family, but less like a getaway. If the beach is the treat, I’d rather book a cancellable oceanfront room and keep Chesapeake as the backup.
Let’s not book yet. I need my sister to confirm whether there’s anything Friday evening. What should I hold in my head as the decision rule?

Use Friday evening as the trigger. If there’s a Friday dinner before about 7, choose the Thursday arrival. If Friday is open, the cleaner Friday one-stop is acceptable, but still not cushy. For lodging: choose oceanfront if you want the weekend to feel like a getaway; choose Chesapeake if the visit logistics and budget win.
Check Richmond quickly too. If it saves enough, maybe.

RIC only helps if the fare gap is big. You’d add about 90-110 minutes of driving to Virginia Beach and still need the rental. For a late Thursday arrival, that drive is the wrong kind of savings. I’d keep ORF unless Richmond is at least $150-$200 less per person.
Okay. Send me the shortlist so I can talk to her and my spouse.

Shortlist: best protected plan is Thursday June 19 DEN-ORF, one short connection, late evening arrival; oceanfront Virginia Beach hotel Thursday-Monday; compact or midsize rental at ORF; Monday midday return. Budget plan is Friday June 20 one-stop arrival around 5 p.m.; Chesapeake hotel; rental; Monday return. Middle plan is Thursday arrival with Chesapeake or airport first night, then oceanfront, but it adds a move. Open items: sister’s Friday timing, whether the beach premium is worth roughly $500-$600, and compact versus midsize rental once you know how much family hauling you’ll do.

Chesapeake: roughly $150-$170 less per night, easier free parking, closer to relatives, still a solid rating with pool and fitness, but no beach stay. Over four nights the practical difference is about $550-$650 once parking and taxes are included.
Let’s do oceanfront. It is the family weekend plus beach. King room, cancellable, balcony request. I know we’re giving up the hot tub.

Good choice for the kind of weekend you described. I have the oceanfront king room Thursday through Monday, cancellable, with pool and fitness access confirmed in the listing, no hot tub, paid parking, and a balcony request added. For flights: Thursday late afternoon from Denver through Washington with about a 70-minute connection into ORF late evening; Monday midday ORF-DEN through Washington. Shall I ticket both travelers?
Yes. Window seats if available, but seated together beats one perfect seat.

Before I lock the car: compact is cheaper and fine for two carry-ons, but midsize is about $45 more and easier if you have checked bags, beach gear, or family errands. Pickup and return would both be at ORF.
Midsize. We always end up carrying folding chairs or food. Use ORF pickup and return.

Done. I booked the Thursday one-stop outbound, Monday midday return, the cancellable oceanfront king room, and the midsize rental at ORF. I placed the balcony and late-arrival notes with the hotel, selected or requested window seats where they were available, and kept adjacent seating ahead of splitting you just for a window.

Booked plan: fly DEN to ORF Thursday June 19 late afternoon with one short connection in Washington, arriving late evening; return ORF to DEN Monday June 23 around midday, also one connection. Stay Thursday-Monday at the oceanfront Virginia Beach hotel in a cancellable king room, with pool and fitness access, no hot tub, paid parking, and balcony request noted. Be at DEN about two hours before departure, keep the airline app open, and if the Denver leg posts more than a 20-minute delay, ask about protection on the next ORF option before you board.
Would you change flights just because of the connection?

Not automatically. I’d only change if there is an earlier Thursday option with a reasonable single connection and no painful fare jump. A much longer layover or an extra stop is not an improvement. For now, keep this itinerary and monitor it closely on travel day.
Parking worries me more because we land late. What should I do with the hotel?

Call the hotel the day before and again Thursday morning: confirm late arrival, ask for the main garage and overflow lot instructions, and restate the balcony request. When you land, go straight to the hotel before any food stop. Keep one overnight bag easy to grab in case you have to use overflow parking.
Return seats got separated after an aircraft swap. There’s only one window left. Take it?

Take the open window now and put the other traveler in the closest same-row or nearby aisle. Then check again right at 24-hour check-in and ask at the ORF counter or gate for adjacent seats. If sitting together becomes more important than the window, be ready to trade the window for two seats together.
Rain is showing for Saturday’s picnic, and rental pickup is after 11 p.m. Any other logistics before I stop thinking about it?

Pack light rain shells and ask your sister for the picnic backup location by Thursday. For Monday, leave the oceanfront hotel around 9:15 a.m., return the car around 10:00-10:15, and head inside for the midday ORF flight. messages.content: I have the next work trip to sort out. It’s a certification workshop in Madison at the end of July for the analyzer software rollout, and I’m not sure whether to fly into Madison or Milwaukee.

Sure. What dates are you working with, and what do you know about the workshop schedule so far? Also tell me whether you want me to optimize for lowest fare, simplest connection, or easiest arrival Sunday night.

Flying from Denver. I think arrive Sunday July 27, workshop starts Monday morning, and it wraps Wednesday afternoon. There’s an optional Sunday evening check-in. I’m fine with one connection, but I don’t want two stops or some long sit. United is fine if it works, but schedule matters more. For hotels, I’d rather be somewhere well reviewed with a pool, hot tub, and gym if that doesn’t make the commute ridiculous.

Got it. I’d compare three practical patterns: Madison through Minneapolis, Madison through Chicago, and Milwaukee with a rental car drive. Since the Wednesday finish is still fuzzy, I’ll flag anything that gets fragile if the final module runs late.
Perfect. Give me the short version first, not every fare on the page.

Best balance: DEN-MSN through Minneapolis on Sunday, leaving Denver around 1:10 p.m. and arriving Madison about 6:25 p.m., with a little over an hour to connect. Return could be Wednesday evening through Minneapolis if the lab ends on time. Roughly $470-$510.

Cheaper but touchier: United through Chicago, Sunday afternoon arrival closer to 7:40 p.m. The Wednesday return has a tight ORD connection, around 40-45 minutes, so I’d be cautious if the practical module can back up. Roughly $430-$470.

Milwaukee: lower airfare, sometimes $310-$360, but then you’re adding a 75-90 minute drive each way. It only saves money if the rental rate stays low and you don’t mind driving after class.
How tight is Wednesday if the workshop ends around 3:30? Madison airport is close, right?

Madison’s airport is close enough—usually 15-20 minutes from the campus area. For a 5:35-ish p.m. MSN departure, you’d want to leave the lab by 3:45 to be comfortable. If the module slips toward 4:15, you’re still not doomed, but it gets rushed. The Chicago return is the bigger concern because the airport arrival may be fine, but the ORD connection leaves very little recovery room.
The optional check-in is supposedly 5 to 7 Sunday. Which option actually gets me there for that?

The Minneapolis-to-Madison option is the only one that gives you a realistic shot at the end of check-in. Arriving around 6:25 means you could probably catch the last portion if bags are quick or if check-in is casual. The Chicago arrival closer to 7:40 likely misses it, and Milwaukee plus the drive almost certainly misses it.
Okay. What about hotel areas? Campus block versus Middleton versus downtown.

Campus block: easiest for the workshop—about a 5-10 minute walk if it’s the UW/campus lab site. It’s around $180-$190 per night, guest score looks fine but not special, and amenities are limited: small fitness room, no real pool/hot tub setup, and parking around $20+ per night.

Middleton suite hotel: stronger guest scores, roughly 4.5-4.6, around $165-$175 per night, free parking, breakfast, fridge, pool, hot tub, and fitness room. Trade-off is a 16-22 minute drive to campus.

Downtown: good restaurants and a nicer evening feel, usually $205-$225 plus paid parking. Fitness is solid, indoor pool at some properties, but hot tub is less likely. Commute is shorter than Middleton by a little, but parking costs make it less clean.

Reserve the convention-center block before the cutoff, with quiet king, away from elevators or ice if possible, and fridge request. Skip the rental car unless your demo kit turns into more than you can reasonably roll into the hotel.
Yes, choose the nonstop on the outbound. Is Friday worth the extra hotel night?

Given the 4:45 possible demo end, yes. A Thursday flight means packed bags, no lingering questions, no post-demo conversation, and a direct dash to the airport. Friday gives you a normal close to the summit and a calmer morning ride to IND. If the fare difference is close, the extra hotel night is buying schedule control rather than luxury.
Okay, Friday. Hotel is my last hesitation. I keep thinking about the no hot tub piece, but walking to everything may matter more.

For this summit, I’d take the block. The suite property is the better wellness-amenity match because it has pool, hot tub, and fitness access, plus the lower rate. But the block keeps you steps from the 8:30 start, badge pickup, reception, and any hallway networking. Since the block still has the pool and fitness room and a decent guest score, the missing hot tub is the trade-off I’d accept here.
Book the block if it’s cancelable until at least a couple days before arrival. Add quiet room away from elevators and a fridge if that’s allowed.

I’ll reserve the block under those terms if available: quiet king, away from elevators/ice, fridge requested, Monday evening arrival noted. I’ll also keep the suite property as the backup until the block confirmation and cancellation language are clear.
Do I need a rental car? I’ll have one demo kit but not a full booth.

No rental car for this version. Airport rideshare to the hotel, then walking for the summit days. Parking would be wasted money, and downtown driving adds more friction than value. If the demo kit gets heavy or awkward, shipping it to the show desk is better than renting a car just to move one case.
Please also make sure I’m not stuck in a middle seat.
Window or aisle for these legs if both are available?
Window if it’s open. Aisle only if the only window is in the last row.

messages.content: Indianapolis is finally off my desk. I need to start looking at the Sacramento clinic loop for October, but the order is still mushy. Can you help me think through flight, hotel base, and car before I commit to anything?
Yes. Give me the rough week and what you know about the sites so far. I can frame it as a few trip shapes rather than pretending the schedule is locked.

Week of October 20. Denver to Sacramento. Monday afternoon setup at a Sacramento reference lab is tentative, Tuesday likely Davis, Wednesday maybe Roseville, and Thursday could be a Stockton install or just a remote recap. I do not want to book until I know the Thursday piece.

There are three sensible flight shapes. First: fly Denver to Sacramento on the Sunday afternoon nonstop, arrive early evening, get the car, and have a calm Monday morning before the lab setup. Second: take a Monday morning nonstop, which saves one hotel night but gives you very little cushion if the flight slips or the lab wants you earlier. Third: use a one-stop itinerary to save money, but that adds risk without helping the training week much. For the return, Thursday evening can work only if Stockton ends on time; Friday late morning or midday is cleaner and costs one extra hotel night.
Price both Thursday and Friday for now. I’d rather not do an ugly connection unless the savings are real. What about where to stay?

For bases, I’d shortlist three. The Roseville suite property is the strongest all-around stay: good guest feedback, free parking, pool, hot tub, fitness room, and rooms with a fridge. It is very convenient for Wednesday and decent for Sacramento, but less convenient for Davis and Stockton. The Capitol-area Sacramento hotel is better geographically for Monday and a little easier for Davis/Stockton, but parking is paid and it does not have a hot tub. The airport hotel only makes sense if you arrive late and want to crash near SMF; I would not use it as the base for the whole loop.
How bad are the drives from Roseville? I can tolerate imperfect if the hotel is better, but I do not want a 90-minute morning every day.

Approximate drive pattern: SMF to Roseville is about 25 to 30 minutes. Roseville to the Sacramento lab is usually 25 to 40 depending on the exact lab address. Roseville to Davis is more like 45 to 60 in the morning. Roseville to Stockton is the stretch, roughly 75 to 90-plus if traffic is unkind. From a Capitol-area hotel, Davis and Stockton are each meaningfully easier, but you trade into paid parking and weaker amenities.
Monday is probably a 1:30 setup, so Roseville after a Sunday arrival might be okay. Davis at 8 on Tuesday is the one that makes me twitchy.

If Davis really starts at 8:00, Roseville means leaving around 6:50 or 7:00 to avoid sweating it. From downtown Sacramento you might leave closer to 7:15. So the question is whether saving 20 to 25 minutes Tuesday morning is worth losing the easier parking and better recovery setup. For one Davis morning, Roseville is still reasonable; I would confirm the Tuesday start time before booking it.
Remind me what the Capitol hotel loses besides parking.

It is closer to the Monday lab and restaurants, but the trade-offs are real: paid parking, no hot tub, smaller room footprint, and the fridge is request-only rather than a reliable suite feature. Guest feedback is fine, not bad, just not as strong as the Roseville suite option.
Roseville sounds less annoying overall. What about the rental? I may have one analyzer case, and if Stockton is live it could be two.

If it is one analyzer case plus your normal bag, a compact could work. If there is any chance of two cases, I’d move to midsize. The price difference is usually modest, and the trunk space matters when you are moving cases between clinic sites. Pickup at SMF on Sunday is straightforward; drop-off timing depends on Thursday versus Friday return.
What do the actual flight times look like?

Representative options: Sunday afternoon nonstop Denver to Sacramento, roughly 2:00 to 3:45 p.m. local arrival, is the cleanest outbound. Monday morning nonstop is roughly 8:30 to 10:10 a.m.; workable only if the lab setup stays at 1:30 and nothing slips. Coming home, a Thursday evening nonstop around 6:30 p.m. is possible after Stockton if you are done by 3:00, but it leaves little room for a late install, gas, car return, and security. Friday late morning or midday is much calmer. The cheaper one-stop returns I’m seeing are not attractive for this week because they push you late and add connection exposure.
I do not want a near-midnight one-stop after Stockton. Keep it on the sheet as a no unless finance starts yelling.

Then my preliminary ranking is: first, Sunday afternoon nonstop outbound, Roseville base, midsize rental, and Friday return if Thursday is truly Stockton. Second, same outbound and hotel but Thursday evening return only if Thursday becomes remote or a very short wrap-up. Third, Monday morning outbound only if the coordinator confirms there is no morning prep, no case pickup, and a forgiving lab arrival window.
Before I commit, give me the confirmation questions for the coordinator. Include whether I actually need to be in Stockton Thursday.

Send this: Can you confirm the final site order for the week of October 20: Monday Sacramento lab setup, Tuesday Davis, Wednesday Roseville, and Thursday Stockton? What are the exact start and expected end times for each site, especially Davis Tuesday morning and Stockton Thursday? For Monday, is 1:30 p.m. firm, and is any morning prep, badge access, or equipment pickup required? For Thursday, do I need to be physically present in Stockton, or can the wrap-up be handled remotely if the install is stable? If Stockton is in person, what is the realistic latest end time? Finally, will I be carrying one analyzer case or two, and are there any site parking or loading dock instructions I should know before booking the rental and hotel base?

ORD is easier, but MDW is fine only if it saves enough to matter. The meeting should end by 11:00, so I can make a 12:30 p.m. or later departure from ORD. Economy is fine, carry-on only. United is nice if comparable, but timing and total cost matter more.

What about staying by the Cleveland airport to save money? I don’t mind rideshares, but I don’t want to make the Wednesday morning annoying.

For flights, is the nonstop premium really worth it? This is such a short hop that a connection feels a little silly, but I’m trying not to overspend.

Flight-only, I would rank them this way:

For ORD-CLE, the connection savings are small enough that I would keep a nonstop unless the fare gap widens.
Thursday should end before noon, but I don’t want to be watching the clock. Which return would you trust?

The United 2:20p from CLE. If the debrief ends at 11:45 or noon near University Circle, a rideshare gets you to CLE around 12:30-12:45, leaving a reasonable cushion with carry-on only. The American 1:30p would work only if the meeting ends early and the car arrives quickly.
Can you pair the United flight with Residence Inn and the cheaper Hampton so I can see the real difference?

The savings are real but not huge once rideshares are included.

Provisional plan: hold or book the refundable Residence Inn University Circle/Medical Center rate if it remains at $184 pre-tax, and keep the United nonstop itinerary as the airfare target. Any issue with the standard king? I was hoping for queen but it’s just me, so not a big deal. I do want to avoid a room without a fridge.

messages.content: Can we start a personal Cleveland weekend? Dec. 12-14 with Daniel. We have Saturday timed tickets at the Cleveland Museum of Art and Sunday lunch with friends before heading back to Chicago. We can leave after work Friday, want one moderate room for two nights, and I’d rather skip a rental car if flying makes sense.
Sure. A few anchors: what time are the museum tickets, where is Sunday lunch, and if you drive would you be leaving right after work or is an earlier Friday departure possible?

Museum is 11:00 Saturday. Lunch is in Ohio City at noon Sunday. Leaving Chicago earlier than 4:30 Friday is unlikely. One room is fine, queen or king; breakfast and a coffee maker/fridge would be nice but not luxury.

Ballpark for two adults, two hotel nights, and transport, not meals or museum tickets:

Plan | Weekend total | Timing | Best part | Trade-off
Fly + University Circle | $980-$1,070 | hotel about 9:30 Fri; Sunday flight after lunch | easiest for museum, no rental | highest cost
Fly + Downtown | $930-$1,020 | same flights | cheaper rooms, more dinner choices | extra ride to museum
Drive + University Circle | $690-$775 | arrive around midnight ET; drive home after lunch | cheapest practical, easiest Saturday | late winter drive
Drive + Downtown | $670-$760 | same drive | slightly cheaper room | higher parking, still commuting to museum
Which hotels are you using for those estimates?

For University Circle, I’d price Glidden House or Courtyard. Glidden often includes breakfast; for either, confirm coffee maker and mini-fridge in the selected room. Parking is usually around $20-$25 per night, and Little Italy gives you easy Friday dinner. Downtown uses Hampton or Holiday Inn Express as the moderate anchors: breakfast is typically included, but parking can run $35-$45 per night.
If we fly, what flights after work actually work?

The clean pattern is ORD-CLE nonstop around 6:30 or 6:45 p.m., landing around 8:50 or 9:00 p.m.; then CLE-ORD Sunday around 3:15 or 4:20 p.m. after lunch. For two tickets, budget $460-$520 before bags or seat fees. Rideshares would be about $35-$40 airport-to-hotel each way and $18-$25 between University Circle and Ohio City.
And driving after 4:30?

Plan on 5.5 to 6.25 hours plus the time change. A 4:30 Chicago departure puts you in Cleveland around 11:45 p.m. to 12:30 a.m. Eastern if weather is normal. Gas and tolls should be about $135-$160 round trip, plus hotel parking.
Does downtown save enough to justify being farther from the museum?

Not really. Downtown may save $40-$70 on the room, but some of that disappears in parking or rideshares to University Circle. Since the fixed Saturday plan is the museum, University Circle is smoother, and Ohio City is still only about 15-20 minutes away Sunday.
Which plan would you pick, and what should I hold?

I’d hold a refundable University Circle room for Dec. 12-14, preferably Glidden House if it is near $200 pretax and includes breakfast. Confirm one queen or king for two adults, cancellation deadline, breakfast, in-room coffee maker, mini-fridge, and parking cost. Then decide drive versus fly closer in: drive if the forecast is fine and the late arrival feels tolerable; fly if two nonstop tickets stay under about $500 or winter weather makes the drive look unpleasant.

My pick is a refundable Glidden House room if it is near $200 pretax. Use Hampton downtown only if late-night dinner access matters more than staying beside the museum.
So the Hampton downtown savings are really only about $60 after parking and museum rideshares?

Right. The room rate gap looks larger, but downtown parking and the Saturday ride to and from University Circle erase most of it. You gain easier downtown dinner and Sunday lunch logistics, but you give up the simpler Saturday morning and the ability to leave the car parked by the museum area.
How much should I value being in University Circle if we're driving and could just park at the museum?

In December, I would value it fairly highly. It avoids moving the car Saturday morning, another garage, and weather timing around the museum entry. Parking at the museum is doable, but the advantage of University Circle is not cost; it is having Saturday feel settled once you arrive Friday night.
What room should I actually reserve?

First choice: Glidden House refundable standard king or standard queen for two adults, non-smoking, at or under about $200 pretax. I would not pay extra for a suite. Add notes for late Friday arrival, parking instructions, and confirmation of included breakfast, in-room coffee maker, and mini-fridge.
If only a standard queen is available, that is fine. I just don't want two doubles.
Agreed. Book the standard queen if that is the available moderate room. I would skip two doubles unless it is the only refundable option left and the price difference is dramatic.
Courtyard is quoting $178. Is that a better reserve than Glidden at $199?

Not if Glidden includes breakfast. Courtyard saves about $42 on room rate over two nights, but two breakfasts can use that up quickly. Courtyard becomes the backup if Glidden has a strict cancellation deadline, parking is higher than expected, or they cannot confirm the fridge.
Then I’ll hold Glidden and keep Hampton downtown as the backup. Anything else before I put the hold in?

Yes: choose the refundable standard queen or king, confirm the cancellation date, ask for written parking cost and garage directions, and save the breakfast plus mini-fridge/coffee notes. It may be walkable depending on the exact address and weather, but for a 9:30 tour I would plan an $8-12 rideshare. That protects the schedule and avoids arriving cold or wet. If the weather is clear, you can decide that morning.
The East End library leg is the bigger concern. No rental still realistic?

What would a rental add?

I don’t need character for this one. One queen is fine; king only if same price.

Will the 2:35 Friday return feel rushed if the debrief ends at noon instead of 11:30?

It is still workable with no checked bag: depart Capitol Square by 12:15-12:20, arrive at RIC around 12:45, and you have roughly 1 hour 45 minutes. messages.content: Hi, I’m Tessa. I’m trying to sketch a September recruitment loop from Salt Lake City through Boise, the Palouse, and Spokane. I need to avoid backtracking if we can. The rough pieces are Boise high-school visits, an evening fair in Nampa, a counselor breakfast near Pullman, and then a Spokane-area fair before I come home.

Absolutely. To make the route workable, can you give me the dates and the fixed event times? Also, is a one-way rental car allowed, or does reimbursement strongly favor returning the car to the same airport?

Travel week is September 16. I have a Monday morning office handoff in Salt Lake, so I’d like to leave after noon. Tuesday is Boise High at 8:15 and a Meridian visit at 10:15, then the Nampa fair from 6:30 to 8:30. Thursday morning is a 7:30 counselor breakfast near WSU in Pullman, then Thursday evening is the Spokane fair. Delta is nice if it’s comparable, but schedule matters more. Coach is fine. I’d rather not do more than one connection, and I don’t want a tiny 35-minute layover.

Given that order, the cleanest routing is Salt Lake City to Boise, then drive north, and fly home from Spokane. Quick comparison: open-jaw SLC to BOI and GEG to SLC gives the least backtracking and a manageable car path, but you may see a one-way rental fee. Boise round trip likely saves some rental complexity but adds a long Spokane-to-Boise return drive at the worst point of the trip. Spokane round trip is the weakest because it front-loads a long drive to Boise before your first school visits.

That’s what I suspected. The Spokane fair is currently Thursday 5:30 to 7:30. I wondered if I could fly home that same night, but I don’t want to be sprinting through the airport with display materials.

Same-night is possible only if there is a late nonstop and the fair ends on time, but it is fragile. You would still need to pack the table, drive to GEG, refuel, return the rental, and clear security. A Friday afternoon return is much more reliable and still keeps the trip to four hotel nights: Monday and Tuesday Boise area, Wednesday Pullman area, Thursday Spokane area.
The Spokane fair is at a venue in Spokane Valley, not downtown. Pullman breakfast is near WSU. I’ll have one suitcase and a couple of small boxes in the car.

Spokane Valley helps, but I still would not make Thursday night the main plan. If the fair ends at 7:30, you might leave the venue around 7:50, reach the airport around 8:20 to 8:30, then still have the car return and security. That is okay for a very late flight, not okay for anything around 9:00. Friday afternoon gives you breathing room and avoids ending the loop on a scramble.
Let’s treat Friday afternoon as the preferred version, but I’d still like to see the Thursday late option as a backup if finance pushes on the hotel night.

Flight shortlist to verify: outbound Monday SLC to BOI, look first at a mid-afternoon nonstop around 2:30 to 4:00 arrival, ideally Delta if the fare is reasonable. That gets you into Boise early enough to pick up the car, check in, and prep for Tuesday. Return option A is Thursday late GEG to SLC, only if there is a nonstop after about 9:45 p.m.; lowest hotel cost, highest stress. Return option B is Friday afternoon GEG to SLC, around 1:00 to 3:30 p.m.; one more hotel night, much better reliability. Return option C is a one-stop Friday itinerary through Seattle, Portland, or Denver; acceptable only if nonstop pricing is bad and the connection is comfortably over an hour.

Hotels are the other piece. Breakfast included helps a lot on school-visit mornings, and I’d like not to be stranded for dinner after the Nampa fair. One queen bed is fine; I don’t need anything fancy.

For the hotel pattern, I’d separate it by the next morning’s first appointment. Boise area for Monday and Tuesday nights, Pullman or Moscow for Wednesday night, and Spokane Valley for Thursday night if you take the Friday return. I’ll favor places with breakfast listed and restaurants close by, but I’d still verify breakfast start times before booking because early visits can expose vague hotel listings.
For Boise, Tuesday morning is Boise High first and Meridian second, then Nampa in the evening. I’d rather not stay all the way in Nampa if that makes the morning annoying.

Best Boise-area fit is probably Hampton Inn and Suites Boise-Meridian or a similar Meridian/I-84 property. It keeps the morning drive reasonable, puts you near restaurants, and makes the Nampa fair an easy evening drive. Hyatt Place near Boise Towne Square is closer to central Boise dining but a bit farther from Nampa, and breakfast can depend on rate or membership. A Nampa hotel is best only if the fair matters more than the morning visits.
For Pullman, I need to be near the WSU-area breakfast by 7:30. I don’t mind Moscow if it’s the better hotel, but I don’t want to start that morning with a surprise drive.

For Wednesday night, Holiday Inn Express Pullman is the straightforward choice if the rate is acceptable: close to WSU and likely the easiest early morning. Best Western Plus University Inn in Moscow is also practical, often has breakfast, and has better nearby dinner options, but you add roughly 15 minutes in the morning. Courtyard Pullman is convenient and has an on-site Bistro, but breakfast may not be included, so it is less ideal unless location or rate wins.
For Spokane, I’m thinking Spokane Valley rather than the airport because of the fair and because I may have one more Friday morning school visit if someone opens a slot.

Spokane Valley makes sense. I’d shortlist Hampton Inn and Suites Spokane Valley, Tru by Hilton Spokane Valley if available, or a similar I-90 property near restaurants. That keeps Thursday after the fair simple and still positions you well for Coeur d’Alene or the airport on Friday. The only thing I would confirm is breakfast start time and whether they have a grab-and-go option if you add that Friday visit.
That gives me enough to take to my director. I’m not ready to book yet; I’ll check the one-way rental fee and the final fair packet. Can you leave me with the route order and risks?

Recommended route: Monday afternoon fly SLC to Boise, pick up a one-way rental at BOI, and stay in Meridian for two nights. Tuesday do Boise and Meridian visits, then the Nampa fair, returning to the same hotel. Wednesday drive Boise/Meridian to Pullman or Moscow and stay near the Thursday breakfast. Thursday attend the Pullman breakfast, drive to Spokane Valley, work the evening fair, and stay in Spokane Valley. Friday fly GEG to SLC, ideally on an afternoon nonstop. Main risks: the one-way rental fee could change the cost comparison; Thursday night return is too tight unless a very late nonstop exists; Pullman-area hotel breakfast times need verification; and the Spokane Valley hotel should be chosen with Friday morning flexibility in mind.

messages.content: Update on the Inland Northwest loop: the Spokane fair moved later, now 7:00 to 9:00 Thursday night, and I added a Friday morning school visit in Coeur d’Alene. So the same-night return is out. Can you revise the return plan and keep it to four hotel nights if possible?

Yes. Four hotel nights should still work if Thursday stays in Spokane Valley and Friday becomes the flight home. What time is the Coeur d’Alene visit, and do you need to check a bag or return display materials with the rental car? That affects how tight the airport timing can be.
Coeur d’Alene High is 8:45 to 9:45 Friday. It could run to 10 if the counselor wants to talk. I’ll have one checked suitcase, the little boxes, and I need to gas up before returning the car at GEG.

Then I’d build around these return choices: 1:00-ish nonstop GEG to SLC is workable only if the visit ends on time and you leave Coeur d’Alene by 10:10; it gives limited lunch and limited recovery from delays. A 3:00 to 3:45 nonstop is the best reliability choice; you can wrap the visit, drive about 50 minutes to the airport area, fuel, return the car, and still not rush. A one-stop route through Seattle, Portland, or Denver only makes sense if the nonstop is badly priced, and I would avoid any connection under about an hour.
Reliability matters more here. I’m fine getting home around dinner, but I don’t want a long layover or a connection that turns a short return into a whole evening.

Then the recommendation is Friday afternoon nonstop from Spokane to Salt Lake, targeting roughly 3:15 p.m. if available. It keeps the four-night structure intact: Monday and Tuesday in Meridian, Wednesday in Pullman or Moscow, Thursday in Spokane Valley. It also gives you enough room for the Coeur d’Alene visit to run a little long without making the airport stressful.
Would the 1:00-ish return be too close if I end up doing a quick debrief after the school visit?

It becomes uncomfortable. If the visit ends at 10:00, a brief debrief can push departure to 10:20 or 10:30. Add the drive to GEG, gas, rental return, and checked-bag cutoff, and the 1:00 flight has very little slack. It is not impossible, but it depends on everything behaving. The mid-afternoon flight is the safer planning choice.
What if the nonstop choices are only morning or evening when I actually book?

Morning would not work with the Coeur d’Alene visit. Evening is acceptable but makes for a long Friday, so I’d compare it against a one-stop itinerary departing early to mid-afternoon with a comfortable connection. If the connection is 60 to 90 minutes and the total travel time stays reasonable, it can be a backup. I would not add a Friday night hotel unless afternoon and evening options both fall apart.
Can you update the hotel sequence with the Friday visit in mind?

Keep Monday and Tuesday in Meridian for the Boise/Nampa segment. Keep Wednesday in Pullman if you want the simplest 7:30 breakfast morning; Moscow is okay only if the hotel value is clearly better. For Thursday, choose Spokane Valley along I-90 rather than the airport. It is better for the late fair, better for the Coeur d’Alene morning, and still reasonable for the airport afterward. Confirm Thursday-night hotel breakfast starts early enough, or plan coffee and a portable breakfast before the school visit.
Great. Give me the revised recommendation in a small summary I can send with the approval note.

Revised recommendation: fly SLC to BOI Monday afternoon, rent one-way from BOI to GEG, stay two nights in Meridian, one night in Pullman, and one night in Spokane Valley. Do not attempt the Thursday night return now that the Spokane fair ends at 9:00. On Friday, do Coeur d’Alene High from 8:45 to about 9:45 or 10:00, then drive to GEG and take a mid-afternoon nonstop to SLC if available. Use a one-stop return only if the nonstop is not viable and the layover is comfortably timed.

messages.content: I’m done enough with the Northwest loop and need to start the Texas one. It’s Oct. 14-17: Monday late-morning counselor meeting near Fort Worth, Monday evening Dallas fair, Tuesday visits in Waco and Temple, and a Wednesday evening alumni event that may be somewhere between Austin and San Antonio. I’m trying to decide open-jaw into DFW and home from AUS or SAT versus a simple round trip. Hotels and rental car are not settled.

This is a north-to-south route, so the simple round trip may make the driving harder. Before I tighten the flight and hotel map, what time is the Fort Worth meeting, the Dallas fair, the Tuesday visits, and do you need to be home Thursday?

Fort Worth is 11:30 near TCU, Dallas fair is 6:30-8:30 at Market Hall. Tuesday: Waco high school at 9:00, Baylor counselor lunch at 11:30, Temple school at 2:15. Wednesday event is likely 6-8 but venue not final. I’d like to be home Thursday, no Friday stay.

Initial read: open-jaw wins unless reimbursement punishes the one-way rental. DFW in / AUS out is the cleanest if Wednesday is Austin or north Austin. DFW in / SAT out is best only if the event lands in San Antonio or New Braunfels. DFW round trip is simple on paper but adds 3+ hours of backtracking Thursday, or a bad late drive Wednesday after the event. AUS round trip is the worst fit because you would have to drive to Fort Worth before the 11:30 meeting. I’d plan DFW in and hold the return airport until the Wednesday venue firms up.
Could I fly in Monday morning, or am I kidding myself and should come Sunday night?

Same-day can work, but only with a nonstop that lands DFW around 9:15 or earlier. You need time to deplane, get the rental car, exit DFW, and drive 35-55 minutes to TCU. A 9:45 arrival is possible on paper but gives you almost no cushion for a late inbound, rental counter line, or Fort Worth traffic. If the clean flight lands after about 9:30, I would move to Sunday night.
Early Monday is fine for this trip. Include Delta if it’s clean, but I’m not taking a weird connection just for the carrier.

Then I’d use a practical flight rule: take the earliest nonstop into DFW that arrives before the buffer cutoff. If Delta has that, great; if Delta connects or lands closer to 10:00, use American or another nonstop into DFW. For the return, Austin usually gives you more workable SLC routings than San Antonio. San Antonio is only worth it if the event is truly south.
Assume no Sunday. How ugly is the road piece if Wednesday ends up Austin versus San Antonio?

If Wednesday is Austin or a north suburb, the route is clean: Dallas after the fair, early Tuesday drive to Waco, Temple after lunch, then continue to Round Rock or North Austin for Tuesday and Wednesday nights. If Wednesday is San Antonio, North Austin becomes a long evening return or a late hotel change; San Marcos, New Braunfels, or north San Antonio would be less painful. The pinch points are Monday DFW-to-Fort Worth after landing, Fort Worth-to-Dallas before the fair, and Tuesday Dallas-to-Waco. For that last one, I’d leave around 6:30 for a 9:00 visit.
I don’t love switching hotels every night. Could I do Dallas Monday and then one southern base Tuesday and Wednesday?

Yes, if the Wednesday venue is Austin, Round Rock, Cedar Park, or even San Marcos. After the Temple visit, you would keep moving south, check into the same hotel Tuesday and Wednesday, and avoid unpacking twice. If the event lands in downtown San Antonio, though, a North Austin base turns into a 90-120 minute drive each way depending on traffic. Then I’d switch the base to San Antonio or use San Marcos/New Braunfels as the compromise.
For hotels, I need to stay inside the university reimbursement range, breakfast included if I can get it, and decent food nearby after the evening events. Nothing fancy.

For Monday, I would not sleep in Fort Worth after the Dallas fair. Look at Dallas Market Center/Medical District, Las Colinas, or North Dallas near the fair, with the deciding factor being late dinner access and a clean route to I-35 for Waco. For Tuesday/Wednesday, if Austin is likely, look at Round Rock, Cedar Park, or the Domain/Arboretum area. Those areas have practical chain hotels, easier dinner options, and breakfast-included rates to verify. If San Antonio becomes likely, shift to New Braunfels or north San Antonio rather than central San Antonio.
My director asked whether staying in Waco Tuesday would make Wednesday easier because Waco hotels may be cheaper. Does that make sense?

Only as a cost play. Waco Tuesday saves some hotel money, but your last Tuesday stop is already in Temple, south of Waco. If you go back to Waco, you push the longer drive into Wednesday: about 1.5-2 hours to North Austin and closer to 3 hours to San Antonio before traffic or setup time. If the venue is likely Austin-area, continuing to Round Rock or Cedar Park after Temple is less stressful.
I can set one Wednesday counselor coffee wherever it helps. The alumni host just has not picked the restaurant yet.

Then place the Wednesday coffee near the eventual hotel base. If you choose Round Rock or Cedar Park, schedule the coffee there or at the Domain and keep Wednesday compact. If the event shifts south, make the coffee in San Marcos or north San Antonio. I would avoid putting the coffee in Waco because it anchors you north and lengthens the event-day drive.
Can you leave me with a plain comparison I can send for approval, including the drive-time risk?

Approval comparison: choose open-jaw unless the one-way rental fee is extreme. Working plan is SLC-DFW early Monday, arriving by about 9:15; pick up a one-way rental; Fort Worth meeting; Dallas Market Hall fair; Monday hotel in Market Center or Las Colinas. Tuesday drive early to Waco, then Temple, then continue south. If the alumni venue is Austin-area, stay Tuesday/Wednesday in Round Rock, Cedar Park, or North Austin and fly home Thursday from AUS. Use SAT only if the venue is south of San Marcos. Main risks: DFW arrival later than 9:30 jeopardizes the Fort Worth buffer; DFW round trip adds a tiring Thursday backtrack; Waco Tuesday is cheaper but moves the long drive to Wednesday.

messages.content: Update on Texas: Wednesday event is confirmed in Cedar Park, 6:00 to 8:00. I need to lock hotel areas. We get reimbursed up to about $185 before taxes. I’m thinking one Dallas-area night Monday and two nights north Austin, but my director still asked if Waco Tuesday is smarter.

Cedar Park simplifies it. I’d use one Dallas-area hotel Monday and one North Austin/Round Rock/Cedar Park hotel for Tuesday and Wednesday. Waco Tuesday only helps the nightly rate; it does not help the flow once your last Tuesday appointment is in Temple.

Monday fair is at Dallas Market Hall until 8:30. The Fort Worth meeting is near TCU. Tuesday is Waco 9:00, Baylor lunch 11:30, Temple 2:15. I’ll need food after the fair and again after the Cedar Park event.

Overnight sequence comparison: A) Dallas Market Center or Las Colinas Monday, then Round Rock/Cedar Park Tuesday-Wednesday: least stressful overall; Tuesday after Temple is about 50-75 minutes to the hotel, Wednesday is local, Thursday AUS is manageable. B) Waco Tuesday, Cedar Park Wednesday: cheaper possibility but adds a hotel change and a longer Wednesday drive. C) Stay south of Dallas Monday to shorten Tuesday: helps the Waco departure a little but usually sacrifices better late dinner choices after the fair. I’d choose A.
For the Dallas night, would you pick Market Center, Las Colinas, or something south toward Waco?

Market Center is best if you want to be off the road quickly after the fair. Las Colinas is a little farther after the fair but often has better chain-hotel value and plenty of restaurants. South toward Waco only makes sense if you are comfortable driving 20-35 minutes after the fair at night and you find a clear breakfast-included rate. My practical pick is Las Colinas if the rate is within cap; otherwise Market Center.
Can you name the hotel styles I should search? I don’t need a luxury place, just predictable.

For Dallas, search Holiday Inn Express, Hampton Inn, Fairfield Inn, or Home2 Suites in Market Center/Medical District and Las Colinas; verify breakfast is included on the rate because some nearby Hilton and Marriott brands charge separately. For the Austin side, search Round Rock/La Frontera, Cedar Park, or the Domain/Arboretum for Hampton Inn, Holiday Inn Express, Home2 Suites, SpringHill Suites, or Fairfield. Round Rock/La Frontera is likely the best price and food balance.
The Domain sounds easy for dinner but maybe over the cap. Would Round Rock make Cedar Park annoying?

No. Round Rock/La Frontera to Cedar Park is typically 20-35 minutes, and after the Temple visit it is an easy continuation south. It also keeps Thursday’s drive to AUS reasonable, usually 35-50 minutes if you leave with cushion. The Domain is nicer for restaurants, but it can cost more and may add traffic. Cedar Park is closest to the event but can be less convenient for the airport.
Okay, please answer the Waco question directly and give me the least-stressful overnight sequence.

Direct answer: do not stay in Waco Tuesday unless the savings are large enough to justify an extra hotel change and a longer Wednesday drive. Least-stressful sequence: Monday night in Las Colinas or Dallas Market Center after the fair, preferably a breakfast-included chain with late dinner nearby; Tuesday morning leave early for Waco; after Temple, drive to Round Rock/La Frontera or Cedar Park and stay there Tuesday and Wednesday; set the Wednesday coffee near that hotel; after the Cedar Park event, return to the same hotel; Thursday fly home from AUS. Round Rock/La Frontera is my first choice if it prices under the $185 cap, with Cedar Park second and the Domain only if the rate is surprisingly good.

messages.content: Last Texas piece: I’m ready to book flights. Delta can do SLC-DFW Monday arriving 9:35, but the return from Austin has a late Atlanta connection and gets me home after 10:30. American has SLC-DFW arriving 9:10 and AUS-DFW-SLC Thursday, home about 4:30, for a little less. Which would you choose?

I’d book American for this trip. The 9:10 DFW arrival gives a better cushion before the 11:30 Fort Worth meeting, and the Austin return gets you home at a sane hour without a long late connection. The Delta return adds fatigue without solving a schedule problem.
The Austin return connection in DFW is 65 minutes. Is that comfortable enough or should I worry?

Sixty-five minutes at DFW on one airline is workable for a domestic connection, but it is not roomy. If there is an 80- to 100-minute connection that still gets you home before dinner, I would pay a modest difference. If the choice is 65 minutes versus the late Atlanta return, I’d still take the 65-minute DFW option.
There is an American return leaving AUS 11:25, DFW 12:35, then DFW to SLC at 2:05, landing 3:55. It’s $32 more.

That is the better itinerary. The 90-minute DFW connection is much more comfortable, and landing in SLC before 4:00 is a strong return. I would book that over both the 65-minute version and the late Delta connection.

Book main cabin rather than basic economy if seat selection or changes matter. Save the fare comparison and note the reason: DFW arrival improves the Fort Worth buffer, AUS return avoids the late Delta connection, and the open-jaw matches the approved DFW-to-Cedar Park route with a one-way rental.

messages.content: I’m starting the next fall loop and need the sane version before I request approval. Late October: Monday counselor breakfast in Eden Prairie, Monday evening fair in Saint Paul, Tuesday visits near Rochester, Wednesday transfer fair in La Crosse, and Thursday morning high school visit in Eau Claire. I’d like to leave SLC Sunday and get home Thursday afternoon if that’s realistic. Should I do MSP round trip and drive the loop, or use a smaller return airport after La Crosse or Eau Claire?

I’d make MSP round trip the baseline. It keeps the flight inventory and rental-car pricing much cleaner. The smaller-airport idea only wins if the exact return has one clean connection and the one-way rental fee is modest. Quick read: MSP round trip is the reliable choice, with a Thursday drive from Eau Claire back to MSP; EAU out shortens the drive but can have thin schedules and fragile connections; LSE or RST out is awkward if you still need to be in Eau Claire Thursday morning.

Dates are Sunday Oct. 27 to Thursday Oct. 31. Eden Prairie breakfast is 8:00 Monday, Saint Paul fair is 6:30-8:30 Monday. Tuesday is Rochester 8:45, Byron 11, and maybe Stewartville at 2. Search Sunday SLC to MSP after 1 p.m., ideally arriving early enough to pick up the car and sleep near Eden Prairie or west Bloomington. The main trade-off is Monday night: either stay near Saint Paul/Eagan after the fair and drive early to Rochester, or drive to Rochester after the fair and make Tuesday morning easier.
I’m okay with one longer post-fair drive, but not two in a row. I also don’t want to roll into a hotel after 11 if I can help it.

Then drive to Rochester Monday after the Saint Paul fair, as long as weather looks normal. If you leave the fair area around 8:50-9:00, Rochester arrival is roughly 10:15-10:30. That keeps Tuesday much calmer. I would not also plan a long late drive Wednesday unless the La Crosse fair stays at 4-6 and you are feeling fresh.
The listed La Crosse conference hotel is expensive. Are Onalaska or downtown La Crosse okay? I need breakfast included if I can get it, and somewhere I can get dinner after the fair.

Both are workable. Downtown La Crosse is better for walkable dinner and anything near the convention center or UWL. Onalaska is better for chain hotels, easier parking, and a simpler highway departure. For included breakfast, Onalaska is more likely to price well. For dinner after a 6 p.m. fair, downtown gives more choices; in Onalaska, verify restaurant hours instead of assuming.
What about flying home from Eau Claire? Is that a trap?

It can be. I would treat EAU as a comparison point, not the plan. The risk is limited flight frequency, a missed connection creating a long delay, and a one-way rental charge. If there is a Thursday early-afternoon EAU option with one comfortable connection to SLC, it is worth pricing. If it involves odd timing, multiple stops, or a big drop fee, MSP round trip is the safer approval request.
Can you sketch the actual overnight sequence if I do MSP round trip?

Baseline sequence: Sunday night Eden Prairie or west Bloomington for the 8 a.m. breakfast. Monday night Rochester after the Saint Paul fair, with late check-in confirmed. Tuesday night La Crosse or Onalaska after the Rochester-area visits, so Wednesday is not rushed. Wednesday night depends on the final fair time and the Eau Claire appointment: Eau Claire if the fair stays 4-6 and Thursday is not too early; La Crosse or a partway stop if either timing tightens.
Could I stay in La Crosse Wednesday and still make the Eau Claire visit?

Yes if Eau Claire gives you 9:30 or later. It becomes tight if they set it before 9, because you would be leaving La Crosse in the dark around 6 or a little after, and breakfast may not be open. This is the one item I’d confirm before locking the Wednesday hotel.
Let’s assume they give me 9:00, and I want a Thursday afternoon departure with a comfortable airport buffer, not a sprint.

For a 9:00 Eau Claire visit, plan to leave the school around 10:15 if possible, drive to MSP, refuel, and return the car around 12:15-12:30. I’d search MSP departures after 2 p.m. That gives a normal airport buffer and avoids depending on a tiny return airport.
Can you make a recommendation now? The reimbursement person wants to know why I’m not using the smaller airport.

Recommendation: request MSP round trip with an MSP-to-MSP rental. Reason: it has the strongest schedule reliability, avoids a one-way rental fee, and still supports a Thursday afternoon return after Eau Claire. Smaller airports should only be used if a specific itinerary appears with one comfortable connection, no punishing layover, and a total cost that beats MSP after the rental fee is included.
And hotel zones in one place, please.

Use these zones: Sunday, Eden Prairie or west Bloomington near I-494 for the 8 a.m. breakfast. Monday, Rochester south or near Apache Mall/Broadway, because you arrive late and need an easy Tuesday start. Tuesday, Onalaska if you want value and easy parking, downtown La Crosse if dinner access matters more. Wednesday, hold flexible until Eau Claire time is firm: Eau Claire for an easy Thursday morning, or La Crosse/partway if the Wednesday fair runs later.
Great. Leave me with a flight-and-car search instruction, not ticketing language yet.

Search SLC to MSP on Sunday Oct. 27 after 1 p.m., prioritizing a clean arrival that leaves time for rental pickup and a normal hotel check-in. Search MSP to SLC Thursday Oct. 31 after 2 p.m. Compare nonstop and one-stop options, but skip anything with multiple connections or a long layover. Rental: MSP pickup Sunday evening, MSP return Thursday around 12:30, and price one EAU-return scenario only as a sanity check.

Look near the I-94 and Highway 54 interchange. Choose a straightforward chain hotel with parking, late check-in, and breakfast listed for 6 or 6:30. Do not pick anything rural or resort-style for this night. Dinner choices there are limited, so treat La Crosse as the reliable dinner stop.

Sunday: west Bloomington or Eden Prairie, close to the Monday 8 a.m. breakfast. Monday: Rochester after the Saint Paul fair; leave the fair area around 8:50-9:00 and confirm late check-in. Change the middle of the loop to avoid a late full drive: keep Monday night Rochester, book Tuesday night Onalaska/La Crosse with included breakfast, and book Wednesday night Black River Falls near I-94/Highway 54. Plan dinner in La Crosse after the 5-7 fair, then drive partway. Thursday leave Black River Falls by 7:00 for the 8:15 Eau Claire visit, then continue to MSP for an afternoon flight.
