messages.content: The PNW loop is put away, so I want to start the Texas swing. Mid-September: Sunday travel from SLC, Monday North Dallas school visits, Monday evening fair in Richardson, Tuesday Fort Worth counselor breakfast, Wednesday Austin school appointments, and Thursday evening San Antonio college night. I’m stuck on open-jaw versus round-trip Dallas, plus hotel bases. I can leave Sunday after lunch, and I’d like to avoid heroic drives after a fair.

Yes. Before I recommend holds, two timing bits matter: what time does the Richardson fair likely release you Monday, and do you need to be back in Salt Lake by any particular time Friday? Also are one-way rental fees reimbursable if the route saves a long backtrack?

Richardson is listed 6:00-8:30 for now. Fort Worth breakfast is 7:30-ish Tuesday. Austin first visit Wednesday should be around 8:30, and San Antonio college night Thursday is 6:00-8:30. Friday I just need to get home at a reasonable hour. Finance will question a one-way car fee but reimburse it if the logic is clear. If Delta is close, include it, but I’m fine with American or Southwest if the schedule is better.

Then I’d frame it this way: option 1, fly into Dallas and home from San Antonio: least backtracking, one-way car, return likely one connection. Option 2, fly into Dallas and home from Austin: sometimes cheaper, but adds a northbound drive after San Antonio or Friday morning. Option 3, Dallas round-trip: may price well, but forces a 4+ hour backtrack. My starting recommendation is option 1 unless the one-way car fee is extreme.
What about starting in Austin on Sunday and driving north? Austin has better flight choices than San Antonio.

I wouldn’t lead with that. Austin-to-North Dallas on Sunday evening is a long wrong-way drive before an 8-ish Monday start, and any flight delay turns into a late hotel arrival plus an early morning. Dallas inbound keeps Monday protected. Between DFW and Love Field, choose the airport that gives the better fare/timing and easiest car pickup; DFW usually makes the one-way rental simpler.

Okay. For the first hotel, I need Monday morning to be painless, and I need somewhere I can still get food after the Richardson fair. Breakfast at the hotel is helpful, but Tuesday has that counselor breakfast.

Use Richardson or Plano for Sunday and Monday. The US-75/George Bush corridor keeps you close to North Dallas schools and the Richardson fair, with late-ish casual food in Richardson/Plano. Addison is workable but adds cross-town driving; downtown Dallas is the wrong base. For Tuesday morning, hotel breakfast may not matter if you’re leaving before 6:00 for Fort Worth, so I’d treat it as useful for Monday only and plan a coffee/protein backup for the car.
Would you move hotels Monday night to Fort Worth after the fair?

Only if that breakfast becomes earlier than listed. After an 8:30 fair, you still have load-out, dinner, and a 50-65 minute drive. A Fort Worth hotel gets you a calmer Tuesday morning, but it creates a late Monday check-in and another unpack/repack. Staying two nights in Richardson means a very early Tuesday departure, but it is simpler and avoids driving tired right after the fair.
Let’s keep the two nights in Richardson for now and flag Fort Worth as a backup if the breakfast time shifts earlier.

Good. The road sequence would be: Sunday arrive Dallas and sleep Richardson/Plano; Monday North Dallas plus Richardson fair; Tuesday leave early for Fort Worth, then drive south after the breakfast/lunch block; Tuesday night Austin; Wednesday Austin schools, then continue to San Antonio; Wednesday and Thursday nights San Antonio.
Hotel areas for Austin and San Antonio?

For Austin, I’d look north/Domain/Arboretum if your Wednesday schools are north or central; it avoids downtown parking and still has easy dinner choices. Use downtown only if the appointments are there. For San Antonio, because the college night is on the north side, airport/North Star or north-central near 410 is more practical than the River Walk. I’d still verify parking cost and breakfast start time, and make sure there are restaurants within a short drive for Thursday after the event.
The Austin list is north and central. San Antonio is near 410, not tourist time. Practical is exactly right.

Then the hotel shortlist is: 1) Richardson/Plano, Sunday-Monday, breakfast listed by 6:30 and parking clear, with a dinner backup after the fair. 2) Austin North/Arboretum or Domain, Tuesday only, free or clearly priced parking, and easy dinner nearby. 3) San Antonio Airport/North Star or north-central 410, Wednesday-Thursday, breakfast at 6:00 or 6:30, parking shown, and restaurants open late enough after Thursday load-out.
For flights, which holds would you put in tonight?

I’d hold three things: Sunday afternoon SLC to DFW/DAL arriving early evening, prioritizing nonstop or clean schedule over a small fare difference; Friday San Antonio-to-SLC in the early afternoon with one comfortable connection; and one backup Friday Austin-to-SLC option only as a price check. I would not hold the Dallas round-trip unless finance specifically asks to see the comparison, because the backtrack is the weak point.
Would you actually keep the Austin return alive?

Yes, but only as a temporary comparison. It is useful if it is dramatically cheaper or has a much better schedule. The hidden cost is the Thursday-night or Friday-morning drive from San Antonio back to Austin, plus possibly returning the car at a different airport than the event city. If the savings are modest, San Antonio return is the cleaner choice.
Car plan? I know one-way rentals can look fine until the taxes and drop fee show up.

Place a cancellable one-way hold for Dallas pickup Sunday around 4:30-5:00 p.m. and San Antonio return Friday late morning. Check the total for drop fee, taxes, unlimited mileage, toll policy, and whether pickup airport changes the rate. Use the same hold to compare DFW versus Love Field only if the flight options are close; otherwise keep the simplest airport.
Give me the action list I can send finance with the why-not-Dallas-round-trip explanation.

Action list: hold Sunday afternoon SLC-Dallas, clean/nonstop schedule; hold Friday early-afternoon SAT-SLC with one comfortable connection; keep an Austin-return hold only long enough to compare; price Dallas round-trip only as benchmark. Hold one-way car Dallas-San Antonio with all fees visible. Hotels: Richardson/Plano 2 nights, Austin North/Arboretum or Domain 1 night, San Antonio Airport/North Star or north-central 410 2 nights. Meal notes: Monday late dinner Richardson/Plano, Tuesday car breakfast before Fort Worth, Tuesday dinner north Austin, Thursday late-dinner backup near 410. Finance rationale: open-jaw avoids the San Antonio-to-Dallas backtrack, protects the Thursday evening event, and reduces fatigue before Friday return.

memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Tessa chose reliability for the Wednesday Austin arrival over a shorter Tuesday drive, kept the two-night Richardson base despite an early Fort Worth departure, and favored returning from San Antonio over saving about $140 through Austin. messages.content: Texas update before I book hotels: Richardson fair now ends at 8:45 p.m., Fort Worth counselor breakfast check-in is 7:15 a.m., and one Austin school can only do first thing Wednesday. Can you rebuild the route? I’m especially unsure about Tuesday night.

With those times, I would not drive all the way to Austin Monday after Richardson. The cleaner structure is still Richardson Sunday-Monday, Fort Worth early Tuesday, then Austin Tuesday night. Before I lock that in: after the Fort Worth breakfast, do you have any Tuesday afternoon visits in North Texas, or can you leave for Austin soon after?
I have one counselor lunch near TCU at noon and should be done by 1:30 or 2:00. No evening Tuesday event.

That helps. Day by day: Monday, stay Richardson after the fair and keep dinner simple. Tuesday, leave Richardson around 5:35-5:45 for Fort Worth, check in at 7:15, do the lunch, then depart about 2:00. That puts you into north Austin roughly dinner time if traffic behaves. Wednesday, sleep near the Austin appointment and leave the hotel around 7:15 for a 7:45 check-in.
Can you compare Austin versus Waco or Temple for Tuesday overnight? I’m tempted by the shorter Tuesday drive.

Tuesday overnight comparison: Austin North/Arboretum has the longest Tuesday drive, but gives the best Wednesday reliability and normal dinner choices. Temple is easier Tuesday, but still leaves an early Wednesday and less margin if I-35 is messy. Waco is the easiest Tuesday, but worst for Wednesday because you are counting on a long morning drive before the school. For an 8:00-ish Austin visit, Austin North is the one I’d keep.

Okay. Return airport is the other question. San Antonio has a Friday flight with one connection that works. Austin is about $140 cheaper, but only if I drive back north after the Thursday evening event or very early Friday.

I’d be cautious about chasing $140 there. A Thursday college night ending around 8:45 means load-out could push you past 9:15, then you still have the San Antonio-to-Austin drive and a late hotel arrival. Friday morning is possible, but it spends your buffer on the highway before a flight. San Antonio costs more but matches the event city and lowers the miss-the-flight risk.
Load-out is likely 20-30 minutes. The event is north side San Antonio, so an airport/North Star hotel would be easy.

Then I’d return from San Antonio. Keep the car through Thursday night, stay north/airport area, fuel before the airport loop Friday, and set the car return for about 10:45 or 11:00 if the flight is early afternoon. Operationally, aim to return it closer to 10:15 so a gas stop or rental line doesn’t eat the buffer.
Where are the breakfast gaps now?

Tuesday is the main gap: Richardson breakfast may open too late for a 5:35 departure, and the Fort Worth event may not serve enough, so carry breakfast. Wednesday at an Austin North hotel should work only if breakfast starts by 6:30 and you leave by 7:15. Thursday and Friday are easier if the San Antonio hotel starts at 6:00, but Friday breakfast cannot push the car-return target.
Late dinners?

Monday: plan a quick Richardson/Plano option or pickup before the fair if dinner service will be thin after 9:00. Tuesday: north Austin/Domain is fine. Wednesday: San Antonio airport or North Star has practical choices. Thursday: assume you may be tired after load-out and save one restaurant that is open until at least 10:00, plus a backup convenience-store meal.
So the hotel sequence stays two Richardson, one Austin North, two San Antonio airport/North Star?
Yes. I’d only change Monday to Fort Worth if that counselor breakfast moves earlier than 7:15. Otherwise the fewer hotel changes are worth the early Tuesday alarm.
What do I need to change from the earlier holds?

Change list: drop the Dallas round-trip as the working plan; keep Dallas inbound and make San Antonio the primary return; keep Austin return only until finance sees the comparison, then release it if the savings stay modest. Set the one-way car as Dallas pickup and San Antonio return. For hotels, keep Richardson Sunday-Monday, choose Austin North/Arboretum over Waco/Temple for Tuesday, and hold San Antonio airport/North Star for Wednesday-Thursday. Add calendar notes: no dependable hotel breakfast Tuesday, protect the Wednesday 7:45 Austin arrival, and do not let Friday breakfast delay fuel and car return.

messages.content: I’m ready to turn Texas holds into reservations. Yes if the Austin hotel is north enough. Before you click, check the exact Tuesday hotel against the first Wednesday school: if it is within about 20 minutes in normal morning traffic, it’s safer than Waco/Temple. What are the hotel area and Wednesday check-in time?

First Austin school is near 183 and MoPac. They want me there at 7:45 for an 8:00 start. The Austin hold is Arboretum area, free parking, breakfast starts 6:30, queen room. Domain option has more restaurants but charges $22 for parking.

Take the Arboretum hold. It keeps Wednesday realistic: breakfast right at 6:30 if you want it, back upstairs quickly, and depart about 7:10-7:15. The Domain dinner scene is nicer, but $22 parking for one night is not worth it unless the room rate is lower by more than that.

For the outbound, the Delta nonstop is also fine if the $36 difference is acceptable; the schedule is close enough that reliability and seat choice can break the tie.

Car: DFW pickup Sunday 4:20 p.m., SAT return Friday 10:45 a.m. The quote shows the one-way fee included. Midsize is cheapest, compact SUV is $9/day more. I’ll have display boxes and banners.

Rooms around San Antonio are disappearing because of the college night. Should I book that before the flights?

Yes, if it is refundable and there’s no prepay penalty, grab the San Antonio room first so you don’t lose the base. Then ticket flights, book the car, and finish Austin and Richardson. Quick comparison: Chicago round-trip is probably cheaper by roughly $150-$250 after fare differences, but it adds a Wauwatosa-to-Chicago backtrack Thursday night or a Friday morning drive to O'Hare, plus tolls and weather risk. Chicago-in/Milwaukee-out may cost more and may add a one-way car fee, but it protects Thursday evening, reduces fatigue, and keeps Friday simpler. I would keep one rental car from Chicago pickup to Milwaukee return; trains and rideshares look fussy for Oak Brook, Madison, and suburban Milwaukee with materials and luggage.
For Chicago, would you aim for O'Hare or Midway?

O'Hare is my first choice because it usually has more SLC afternoon choices, more rental inventory, and an easier angle to Oak Brook. For the car, the one-way fee is acceptable if it is visible upfront and not much over the cost of the extra gas, tolls, and time of backtracking.

Outbound Sunday: shortlist a 1-3 p.m. SLC to O'Hare nonstop if the fare is reasonable; a similar United or American nonstop is fine if it lands earlier or costs materially less; keep a Midway option only as a price check. Ranking for now: first, a late-morning or early-afternoon MKE-SLC one-stop with about 70-100 minutes to connect; second, a midafternoon MKE-SLC with a longer but not absurd connection if the first option gets too tight; third, driving to O'Hare for a cheaper or nonstop return; last, a pre-8 a.m. Milwaukee departure or any two-stop routing. Oak Brook: look at Oakbrook Terrace or Oak Brook proper near the fair, with free parking and food nearby; Hyatt House, Hilton Garden Inn, or a comparable Marriott/Hilton property would be practical. messages.content: I’m switching back to work travel. I have a late-February Front Range yield loop: Wednesday 7:30 counselor breakfast near Boulder, Wednesday 6:30 admitted-student reception near Denver Tech Center, Thursday 8:15 setup for a transfer fair in Aurora, and a Thursday 5:30 alumni counselor meetup in Fort Collins. Can you help me decide fly versus drive and where to hold hotels?
Absolutely. Two things affect the reliability of this one: when can you leave Salt Lake on Tuesday, and do you need to be home Thursday night or is Friday morning acceptable?
I can leave Tuesday after 1:00. Friday morning is acceptable. I’d only try Thursday night if it’s genuinely clean, not a sprint from Fort Collins to the airport.

Then I’d compare it this way:

Fly + rental: fastest, avoids the long winter I-80 drive, and gives you a car for the scattered events. Best if you arrive Tuesday afternoon or early evening.

Drive from Salt Lake: more flexible with materials and no rental counter, but it adds a full winter driving day each way and gives you less margin if weather turns.

Given the 7:30 Wednesday breakfast and the late Thursday Fort Collins event, flying Tuesday and returning Friday is the cleaner planning base.
I’m leaning fly unless the rental makes it silly. Could I survive with one hotel base, or is this a split-nights trip?

One base is possible, but not elegant. Broomfield/Westminster is the least-bad single base: reasonable for Boulder, not awful to DTC/Aurora, and north enough for Fort Collins. The downside is you’d be doing a late drive back north after the DTC reception and then an early drive southeast to Aurora.

Split nights reduce risk: Tuesday near Boulder/Broomfield, Wednesday near DTC/Aurora, Thursday near the airport after Fort Collins for a Friday flight.
Three hotels is annoying. What about Broomfield Tuesday and Wednesday, then airport Thursday?

That cuts one check-in, but Thursday morning becomes the weak spot. From Broomfield to an 8:15 Aurora setup, you’d want to leave quite early and still carry traffic risk. Since the DTC reception ends around 8:00 or later Wednesday, moving to a DTC/Aurora hotel that night makes Thursday much calmer.
The DTC reception is scheduled to end at 8:15. You’re right; I don’t want a pre-dawn traffic gamble to Aurora.

Then I’d use this driving pattern: Tuesday fly in, pick up rental, sleep Boulder/Broomfield. Wednesday breakfast near Boulder, midday work block, then drive south before peak traffic and stay DTC/Aurora after the reception. Thursday do the Aurora fair, drive to Fort Collins midday with a lunch stop, then after the 5:30 meetup either stay near the airport or, if the flight is later Friday, stay north and drive down in the morning.
Please shortlist hotels by area. Breakfast helps, and dinner access matters after the reception. Nothing fancy.

Shortlist to check first:

Boulder/Broomfield Tuesday: Hyatt House Boulder/Broomfield or a Hampton/Residence Inn in Broomfield-Interlocken. Look for included breakfast, easy parking, and nearby casual dinner.

DTC/Aurora Wednesday: Hyatt Place Denver Tech Center, Hampton Inn Denver Tech Center South, or a practical Aurora South hotel near the fair site. Favor whichever is closer to the Thursday venue and has food within a short drive.

Airport Thursday: Hampton/Hyatt Place-style options in Gateway Park or Peña Station. They usually make Friday morning rental return simpler than sleeping deep downtown.
If you had to hold only a couple refundable rooms now, which ones?

Hold one Broomfield/Interlocken room for Tuesday and one DTC/Aurora room for Wednesday. I’d wait on the Thursday airport room until flights are narrowed, unless the refundable rate is painless. The first two nights are driven by event timing; Thursday depends on whether the Friday return is early or late morning.
Good. For flights, I do not want a connection on Salt Lake to Denver unless something is really off.

Agreed. For this route, target a nonstop Tuesday after 1:00 that lands with enough daylight and rental-car buffer. I’d avoid the last flight of the night. For Friday, a midmorning nonstop gives you time to return the rental without making the airport hotel feel pointless.
Delta if it’s close, but don’t pay a big premium. And window seat if I can choose it.

Got it. I’ll compare nonstop options by timing and price, with Delta favored only if it’s comparable. I’ll also note whether a window seat can be selected at booking or whether it has to wait until check-in.
Can you give me the practical version to send myself? I don’t need booking language yet.

Practical plan: fly SLC to Denver Tuesday afternoon after 1:00, rent a car, and avoid connecting flights. Hold Tuesday night in Broomfield/Interlocken for the Boulder breakfast. Move south Wednesday afternoon and hold Wednesday night near DTC/Aurora so the Thursday 8:15 setup is low-stress. After the Aurora fair, drive to Fort Collins with a lunch buffer before the 5:30 meetup. Tentatively plan Thursday night near the airport for a Friday midmorning nonstop home, but finalize that once fares and return times are checked. For hotels, prioritize included breakfast where it actually helps and easy dinner access after the DTC reception.

It is more packing, but the hotel changes follow the route instead of fighting it.

For Fort Collins, do not leave Aurora hungry or right at the last possible minute; northbound traffic can look fine and then clog. I’d rather you arrive early and answer email in the car than eat the whole buffer on I-25.

Clean plan: first, hold Tuesday in Broomfield/Interlocken with free parking and breakfast if available. Second, hold Wednesday in Aurora/Anschutz; use DTC only if Aurora rates are ugly. messages.content: Denver is wrapped enough that I need to start the Pacific Northwest loop. Tuesday morning counselor breakfast in Salem, Tuesday evening admitted-student reception in Beaverton, Wednesday transfer table in Vancouver, Washington, and Wednesday evening alumni meetup near Tacoma. Can you compare Portland round-trip versus flying into Portland and home from Seattle, and help me figure out hotel areas? I want breakfast and late dinner logistics not to be chaotic.

Yes. The airport decision is mostly about the end of the loop, not the start. Portland round-trip is usually simpler for the rental car, but after the Tacoma meetup it creates either a late 2.5 to 3 hour drive back toward Portland or a very early Thursday airport morning. Portland-in and Seattle-out adds a one-way car return, but it fits the actual route much better. Before I rank it too hard: what time can you leave Salt Lake on Monday, and when do you need to be back Thursday?
I can leave Monday after a noon meeting, so afternoon is best. Thursday I need to be back by late afternoon. If Delta has a sensible option, include it, but not if the connection is worse.

Then I would look first at a Monday afternoon nonstop SLC to PDX, roughly a 1:30 to 3:30 departure window, on Delta or Alaska if the times work. For Thursday, the cleaner target is a SEA to SLC nonstop late morning or early afternoon. I would only use a Portland return if it saves real money, roughly $250 or more after the one-way rental fee, or if the Seattle return forces a bad connection.
What does the driving pattern look like? I am undecided on whether Salem the first night is worth the extra hotel move.

Basic route: PDX to Salem Monday is about 1 hour to 1 hour 15 if you land before the worst evening traffic. Salem to Beaverton after the Tuesday breakfast is usually 55 to 75 minutes. Beaverton to Vancouver after the reception is 35 to 45 minutes later in the evening. Vancouver to Tacoma on Wednesday can be 2 to 2.5 hours depending on I-5. Tacoma to SeaTac after the meetup is usually 35 to 45 minutes. If the Salem breakfast check-in is early, Salem Monday is worth it. If breakfast starts later, Beaverton or Tigard Monday could reduce one move, but it makes Tuesday morning more fragile.
The Salem check-in may be 7:30. Beaverton probably ends around 8:30 p.m. Tacoma is likely done around 8-ish, but not confirmed.

With a 7:30 Salem check-in, I would protect Tuesday morning. My practical plan is: Monday night in Salem, Tuesday night either Vancouver or north Portland, Wednesday night near SeaTac. It is three hotel nights in three places, which is annoying, but each drive has a purpose and you avoid the worst late-night backtrack. The risky version is Portland round-trip plus a Wednesday night drive south after Tacoma; I would not choose that unless the price difference is large.
Could Tuesday night be Beaverton instead of Vancouver so I am not packing up after the reception?

It can. Beaverton Tuesday is easier immediately after the reception: short drive, quicker dinner, simpler check-in. The trade-off is Wednesday morning from Beaverton to Vancouver, which can be 35 to 60 minutes with bridge traffic and parking time. Vancouver Tuesday is better if the transfer table has an early setup or if parking on that campus is fussy. Beaverton Tuesday is better if the event runs late or the host adds a dinner.
Food is the thing I do not want to scramble over. Breakfast hours too, especially Salem.

For Salem, only hold a hotel where breakfast is listed at 6:00 or 6:30 and the venue is within about 15 minutes. If breakfast starts at 6:30 and check-in is 7:30, still buy yogurt or a bar Monday night as a backup. For Beaverton after the reception, use Cedar Hills Crossing, downtown Beaverton, or Washington Square as dinner fallbacks, but check closing times because 8:45 can be late for a full meal. For Vancouver, the waterfront has better restaurants but more parking friction; Jantzen or Delta Park is easier for parking but thinner on late food. After Tacoma, eat near the meetup if it ends on time; otherwise drive to SeaTac and use an airport-area late option or hotel bistro.
Which areas should I actually hold tonight while the hosts are still confirming exact times?

Hold refundable rooms in three buckets. First, Salem near I-5, Commercial Street, or Mill Creek for Monday, with easy parking and breakfast verified. Second, hold two Tuesday possibilities for now: Beaverton or Cedar Hills if Tuesday comfort matters more, and Vancouver, Jantzen, or downtown Vancouver if Wednesday setup timing becomes tight. Third, hold SeaTac or Angle Lake for Wednesday night rather than downtown Tacoma, because it protects the Thursday flight without making you drive all the way back to Portland.
What about Salem Monday, Beaverton Tuesday, and SeaTac Wednesday? That feels logical on the map.

That is a reasonable sequence if the Vancouver table starts late morning. It gives you the best Tuesday evening recovery: finish Beaverton, eat nearby, sleep nearby. The only exposed piece is Wednesday morning Beaverton to Vancouver, especially if you need to unload materials before a before-lunch table. If Vancouver setup is 10:30 or later, I am comfortable with Beaverton Tuesday. If it is before 9:30, I would switch Tuesday to Vancouver or Jantzen.
The Vancouver time is not confirmed. I only know Wednesday sometime before lunch.

Then hold both Tuesday options for a couple of days: one Beaverton or Cedar Hills room and one Vancouver or Jantzen room, both refundable. Put cancellation reminders a day before each deadline. Once Vancouver confirms, release one. I would not let that uncertainty keep you from choosing the Seattle return if the fare is reasonable; Tacoma already makes Seattle the cleaner exit.
Can you give me a clean shortlist with the flight choice, hotel holds, and what would change your mind?

Clean shortlist: first choice flight is SLC to PDX Monday afternoon, then SEA to SLC Thursday late morning or early afternoon, nonstop if available. Use Portland round-trip only if Seattle return plus the one-way car fee is more than about $250 higher or the SEA flight forces an awkward connection. Rental car: pick up at PDX Monday and return at SEA Thursday. Hotel holds: Monday Salem I-5 with breakfast verified; Tuesday hold both Beaverton/Cedar Hills and Vancouver/Jantzen until the transfer-table time lands; Wednesday SeaTac or Angle Lake. Decision triggers: keep Salem Monday if breakfast check-in stays before 8:00, choose Vancouver Tuesday if setup is before 9:30, and keep SeaTac Wednesday if Tacoma ends after 8:00.

That is now clearly the best fit because Tacoma ends late enough that you do not want to drive back toward Portland. 2) Portland round-trip with a Thursday morning drive from SeaTac/Tacoma down to PDX, but only if the savings are large. 3) Portland round-trip with a Wednesday night drive after Tacoma. So Portland round-trip is basically out unless the price blows up?

Correct. With an 8:15 Tacoma end, Portland round-trip either gives you a late-night long drive or a very early Thursday drive before a flight. If the Seattle return plus one-way car fee is within roughly $200 of Portland round-trip, I would take Seattle and protect the end of the trip.

Leave Salt Lake by 10:00. Build in one real stop and target Twin Falls by 2:30 to 3:00, which gives you a cushion before 4:30. Ceremony is by Sac State. Relatives are mostly Carmichael and Fair Oaks. Sofia is out around 3:15 and Marco can be home by 4. We need a real two-queen room, not a sofa-bed setup, and breakfast at the hotel would help.

For Pearl Street at 7:30, I would lean Boulder if the rate is acceptable. If Boulder is overpriced, use Louisville or Superior rather than Longmont; you stay on the right side of the commute and still avoid some Boulder parking pain. Since breakfast is part of the event, hotel breakfast that morning matters less.

If the display bag is checked-size, I would avoid making it the only copy of your materials. Put essentials in your carry-on: visit folder, name tags, QR sheet, and a small brochure stack. Ship a non-critical box to the first hotel or Fort Collins host, and include a return label if you can.

Then fly-and-rent still works. Ask the Sunday hotel to accept packages under your name and arrival date, and confirm any handling fee. Keep Monday-critical items with you. If the office wants the full fair kit every day, driving becomes more attractive, but for one shipped box plus carry-on essentials, flying is fine.

Sunday: Fort Collins or Loveland. Monday: Boulder, or Louisville/Superior if Boulder is too expensive. Tuesday: DTC or Greenwood Village. Wednesday: Colorado Springs north if you want better dinner choices and a short drive after the school visit; Pueblo if you want the easiest Thursday morning. In the approval note, flag package acceptance at the Sunday hotel, parking costs in Boulder and DTC, and meals: event breakfast Tuesday, easy DTC dinner Tuesday, and a simple Wednesday dinner in Colorado Springs or Pueblo.

Dinner after the fair: I do not want to wander downtown with the banner.

Then make dinner a hotel-area plan. After the fair, load out, go straight back to Greenwood Village, and eat at one of the restaurants next to the Hampton or place a mobile order before leaving the garage. Budget parking as: hotel $16 total, downtown fair garage about $25-35, Union Station garage about $12-20. messages.content: Colorado is wrapped up and I’m starting the mid-September Pacific Northwest loop. Draft schedule is Sep 15-19: Monday 7:30 counselor breakfast in Vancouver, WA, Monday evening Portland fair, Tuesday school visits around Salem, Wednesday 1:00-4:00 transfer fair in Eugene, and Thursday 10:30 counselor coffee near Corvallis. I need a route comparison before I ask for approval: fly-and-rent, open-jaw, or drive the whole thing from Salt Lake.

I can rank those. A few details will affect whether the open-jaw is worth it: how much material are you taking, are you okay flying out Sunday afternoon, do you need to be home Thursday night, and will the office allow a one-way rental if the fee is reasonable?

Two boxes of brochures plus the pop-up banner. I can ship one box to the first hotel, but not the banner. Sunday afternoon is fine. I’d like to be home Thursday night. A one-way rental is okay if it is not ridiculous.

First pass: 1) Fly SLC-PDX Sunday, rent, return from EUG Thursday: least backtracking, best if the EUG return has one comfortable connection; watch the one-way car fee and smaller-airport disruption risk. 2) Fly SLC-PDX round trip, rent and return at PDX: simplest flights and rental, likely cheaper, but adds the Corvallis-to-PDX drive Thursday after coffee. 3) Drive SLC-Vancouver-Salem-Eugene-Corvallis-SLC: maximum material control and no flight risk, but two very long travel days and probably more fatigue than savings. My practical primary would be to price 1 and 2 side by side; keep 3 as backup only if shipping or fares fail.
I’m not excited about a tiny Eugene connection. If the return from Eugene has one short layover that is 70 minutes or more, fine. If it is a 40-minute scramble, I would rather drive back to Portland.

Good boundary. Approval version: open-jaw wins only if the Eugene return has one connection with about 70-75 minutes or better and gets you to SLC Thursday evening. If the connection is tighter, choose the Portland round trip even though it adds the drive. The full-drive plan should not be the requested plan unless the material load grows.
Sketch the actual Sunday-to-Thursday routing for the two flight versions.

Open-jaw route: Sunday fly SLC-PDX, pick up car, sleep Vancouver or north Portland. Monday breakfast in Vancouver, Portland fair, then drive to Salem for the night. Tuesday Salem visits, then drive to Eugene. Wednesday Eugene fair, then sleep Corvallis if the Thursday coffee is there and the Eugene flight is late enough; otherwise stay Eugene. Thursday Corvallis coffee, drive to EUG, drop car, fly home. Portland round trip: same through Wednesday, but after the Thursday coffee drive Corvallis-PDX, return the car there, and fly home late afternoon or evening.
Where would you put the hotels? I am fine switching, but I do not want to end up with a pretty hotel that makes the first visit harder.

Hotel areas I’d use: Sunday Vancouver waterfront, downtown Vancouver, or Jantzen Beach/north Portland so Monday breakfast is easy and Portland fair access is still reasonable. Monday Salem or Keizer near I-5, because Tuesday starts there. Tuesday Eugene near the university, Valley River, or north Eugene, depending on the transfer fair site. Wednesday Corvallis if the Thursday coffee is definitely near Corvallis; Eugene only if the flight home forces it.
Is it dumb to drive to Salem after an 8:00 pm Portland fair?

Not dumb, but plan it deliberately. Eat before leaving Portland or stop in Wilsonville/Woodburn, then check into a Salem/Keizer hotel with late desk coverage. It buys you a calmer Tuesday morning. Staying in Vancouver Monday night would make Tuesday too dependent on early traffic.
Breakfast and parking need to be in the approval note. The school visits start early enough that I do not want breakfast to be a mystery.

Add hotel criteria rather than specific brands for now: breakfast confirmed by 6:30 in Vancouver/north Portland and Salem, and by 7:00 in Eugene/Corvallis; parking either included or a stated nightly amount; interior storage or front-desk hold for shipped materials. If a hotel cannot confirm breakfast hours, assume a coffee-and-bagel receipt instead of relying on it.
Dinner access too, especially Monday after Portland and Wednesday after Eugene.

Monday dinner: pre-fair early dinner in Portland, or a quick stop on I-5 before Salem. Choose a Salem hotel near restaurants, not an isolated highway exit. Wednesday: if staying Corvallis, pick downtown or riverfront-adjacent so you can get food after the Eugene fair without another drive. If staying Eugene, Valley River or campus-area hotels usually make dinner simpler.
How should I handle materials?

Ship one brochure box to the first hotel for arrival by Saturday and have the label include your name, university, arrival date, and hold for guest. Carry the banner and one core packet set. Each morning, take only that day’s materials; keep extras covered in the cargo area, and never leave the laptop or badge bag in the car.
Can you turn this into a sign-off note with the three options and the recommendation?

Draft sign-off note: For Sep 15-19 Pacific Northwest recruitment loop, request pricing for two flight plans. Preferred if reliable: fly SLC-PDX Sunday afternoon, rent a car, complete Vancouver-Portland-Salem-Eugene-Corvallis route, return from EUG Thursday after the 10:30 Corvallis coffee, only if the return has no more than one comfortable layover and the one-way rental fee is reasonable. Fallback: fly SLC-PDX round trip, same rental from PDX, drive back to PDX after Thursday coffee, and fly home late Thursday. Backup only: full drive from Salt Lake City with materials, used if shipping or fares make flying impractical. Hotel plan: Sunday Vancouver/north Portland, Monday Salem/Keizer, Tuesday Eugene, Wednesday Corvallis unless flight timing favors Eugene. Approval needs to include hotel breakfast hours, parking costs, late dinner access, material hold or shipping fees, fuel, and one-way rental fee if applicable.
One focused revision: if the Eugene return prices well but has a 43-minute layover in Seattle, should I still list it?

No. List that as priced but not recommended. The approval ask should say: choose EUG return only with a connection around 70-75 minutes or longer; otherwise approve the PDX round trip despite the extra drive. For arrival reliability, a cheap 43-minute connection out of Eugene is not worth building the loop around.

messages.content: The PNW hosts finally firmed up times. Salem moved earlier Tuesday, Eugene confirmed the Wednesday transfer fair ends at 8:30, and Corvallis is still Thursday late morning. Can you rank the flight/routing plans and tell me where I should actually sleep?

Yes. The key trade-off is Thursday: an Eugene return saves driving after Corvallis, but only if the connection is not rushed. Send me the flight quotes you have and I will rank them with the hotel bases.

Option A is SLC to PDX Sunday afternoon, then EUG to SLC Thursday with a 43-minute Seattle layover, $456. Option B is PDX round trip, Sunday afternoon in and Thursday 5:15 pm back, $392. Option C is the same open-jaw but the EUG return has a 78-minute Seattle layover, $486. Rental is about $40 more for one-way drop at EUG.

My ranking: 1. Option C, open-jaw with the 78-minute Seattle layover. It costs more, but it protects Thursday and avoids the Corvallis-to-Portland drive before a flight. 2. Option B, PDX round trip. Use this if reimbursement pushes back on the higher airfare and one-way rental. The drawback is a long drive after the Corvallis coffee, with Portland traffic uncertainty. 3. Option A, cheaper EUG return with 43 minutes in Seattle. I would list it only as priced but not recommended.
Okay. For Sunday and Monday, would you stay near the Portland fair venue or in Vancouver? The venue hotels have paid parking and no breakfast, but Vancouver adds traffic.

I would stay Vancouver or north/east Vancouver Sunday and Monday, then plan the Monday fair drive deliberately. Since you have the Vancouver counselor breakfast Monday, the free breakfast and parking are useful, and you can avoid moving hotels that day. For the Portland fair, leave the hotel early, preselect a garage near the venue, and treat the parking fee as part of the fair cost. I would only switch to a venue hotel if load-in is unusually early or parking becomes impossible.
Tuesday night is the bigger question. Salem/Keizer after the morning visits, or push to Eugene?

Push to Eugene Tuesday night. Because Salem starts early, you should be done early enough to drive south before dinner. Staying in Eugene Tuesday gives you a calmer Wednesday, lets you check the fair location ahead of time, and avoids a morning I-5 drive with materials in the car.
What about breakfast timing before the early Salem visit?

For Tuesday, choose the Vancouver hotel only if breakfast starts by 6:00 or has grab-and-go available by 6:30. If not, plan a coffee-and-bagel stop on the way to Salem. For Eugene, breakfast is more useful Wednesday and Thursday, but Thursday you should keep it quick because of the Corvallis coffee.
Which refundable rooms should I hold first while approval finishes?

Hold these in order: first, a Vancouver-area hotel for Sunday and Monday with free parking, breakfast, and a queen non-smoking room. Second, an Eugene or Springfield hotel for Tuesday and Wednesday with breakfast, easy parking, and restaurants close enough for after the Wednesday fair. Third, a backup Portland venue hotel for Monday only, refundable, in case the organizer later says load-in or parking will be difficult. I would not hold Salem unless the Tuesday schedule runs much later than expected.

Recommendation: approve SLC-PDX Sunday afternoon and EUG-SLC Thursday with the 78-minute Seattle connection, plus the one-way rental drop at EUG. Do not use the 43-minute connection. Hotel plan: Vancouver-area base Sunday/Monday for the counselor breakfast and parking/breakfast value; Eugene/Springfield Tuesday/Wednesday to protect the Wednesday fair and Thursday Corvallis timing. messages.content: Back from the Oregon loop and I already have the next puzzle. Can you help me shape an early October North Texas route before I send it for approval? Yes. A few details affect whether the routing is truly workable: how many materials are you moving, what hotel or airfare caps should I keep in mind, and do you have Sunday or Thursday flight-time limits?

Probably five boxes plus the banner tube if I don't ship. Hotel cap is $185 before tax unless there's a reason. Airfare can be higher if it saves real staff time. I can leave Sunday afternoon but not morning. Thursday meeting should be done around noon; I'd rather not get back to Salt Lake near midnight. One easy connection is fine.

Initial read: open-jaw is the plan to defend. Option 1, SLC to Dallas and Austin back to SLC, follows the route south and avoids a Thursday backtrack; the trade-offs are possible higher airfare, a one-way rental fee, and a materials plan. Option 2, Dallas round trip, may price cleaner and avoids a car drop fee, but Round Rock back to DFW is about 3 to 3.5 hours before traffic, so any late meeting or I-35 slowdown makes the return less reliable. Option 3, driving from Salt Lake, solves materials but costs multiple travel days and fatigue; I would only use it if flying plus shipping becomes impossible.
Can you sketch the overnight areas? I can handle three hotels if it actually helps, but I don't want to make a mess.

I would use three hotel areas. Sunday and Monday: Plano, Richardson, or Addison, not downtown Dallas. That protects the Plano breakfast and gives better odds of free parking and breakfast under the cap. Tuesday: either Fort Worth south/Arlington if the visits run late, or Waco if you can leave Fort Worth by mid-afternoon. Wednesday: Round Rock or Georgetown after the Waco fair if the fair really ends around 5. That puts you close to Thursday's meeting and Austin airport.
The Dallas fair load-in starts 4:30 and ends at 8:30. I am a little worried about downtown parking with boxes.

Then I would not pick an over-cap downtown hotel just to be near the fair. Stay north where parking and breakfast are simpler, then pre-reserve a garage or official event lot for Monday from about 3:30 to 9:15. Leave Plano/Richardson by 3:15. Also choose an SUV or at least a vehicle with covered cargo space so the boxes are not visible while you are at dinner or between visits.
What if I fly into Love Field instead? Does that reduce the Monday pain?

Love Field can work if the fare and arrival time are good, but it does not change the route enough to chase it. It is a little easier for central Dallas, while DFW usually has stronger SLC nonstop options and is fine for Plano/Richardson. I would compare both Dallas airports, but I would not give up a good DFW Sunday afternoon nonstop for a weaker Love Field connection.
For materials, I don't know if I should check, ship, or drive.

I would not drive from Salt Lake just for five boxes. Best plan: ship the heavy brochures to the first confirmed receiving point, ideally the Monday fair or the first hotel if they will accept packages without a big handling fee. Carry the scanner, tablecloth, small counselor packets, and anything irreplaceable. If you must fly with the banner tube, treat it like a checked item and keep the receipt. After Dallas, keep remaining materials in the SUV for Waco and Round Rock.
How bad is the Dallas round trip if we need cheaper airfare?

It is not impossible, but it is the weaker operational plan. After a late-morning Round Rock meeting, you would drive north to DFW, refuel, return the car, and clear security before an evening flight. That is a long final day and leaves little buffer if the meeting runs over or I-35 is slow. I would only switch to Dallas round trip if Austin return pricing is dramatically worse or if the Austin options require multiple stops, long layovers, or a very late Salt Lake arrival.
Breakfast and dinner access matter because the days are going to be weird. Flag that in the approval note.

For hotel areas, I would write it this way: North Dallas/Plano-Richardson for Sunday and Monday because it supports the Plano breakfast, has free-parking hotels under cap, and still works for the Dallas fair with pre-reserved event parking. Waco Tuesday if you can reach it after Fort Worth, because it reduces the Wednesday transfer-fair scramble. Round Rock/Georgetown Wednesday because it protects Thursday morning and has easier dinner options than arriving late from Waco on Thursday morning.

Approval recommendation: approve open-jaw air into Dallas and out of Austin, plus a one-way SUV rental. The trip moves south from Plano/Dallas to Fort Worth, Waco, and Round Rock, so returning from Austin avoids a 3-plus-hour Thursday backtrack to DFW after the final meeting. Hotel plan is two nights in Plano/Richardson, one night in Waco, and one night in Round Rock/Georgetown, prioritizing included breakfast and free or simple parking under the $185 pre-tax cap. Last thing: if Austin return options are terrible, what would you check before switching back to Dallas?

A late nonstop is a backup if the price is reasonable, but it creates a long airport wait or a late night. I would switch back to Dallas only if Austin is several hundred dollars higher after the one-way car fee, or if the only Austin options are unreliable connections. For refundable room holds once dates are firm, start with Plano/Richardson for Sunday/Monday, Waco for Tuesday, and Round Rock/Georgetown for Wednesday.

Returning from Dallas would add a 3-plus-hour Round Rock-to-DFW backtrack after the Thursday meeting, plus fuel, tolls, extra driving time, and return-flight risk. Standard SUV is needed for five boxes and a banner tube; one-way fee is documented. Hotels are under the $185 pre-tax cap and include breakfast and free parking. Final itinerary: Sun Oct 6 Delta SLC-DFW 3:10-6:45, window requested; pick up standard SUV at DFW 7:15 pm; Hampton Plano-Richardson Sun/Mon. Tue Oct 8 Fort Worth visits, evening Waco fair, Holiday Inn Express Waco South. Wed Oct 9 reposition to Round Rock, Hampton Round Rock-La Frontera. Thu Oct 10 Round Rock meeting, return SUV at AUS 1:30 pm, American AUS-PHX-SLC 3:05-7:45, windows requested. Save airfare receipt, Dallas-return comparison, rental receipt, fuel/tolls, hotel folios, Dallas parking, and any materials shipping or baggage receipts.

memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Tessa kept the Dallas garage reservation with the new load-in entrance plan, chose a grab-and-go breakfast backup for Waco, accepted the adjusted Austin-Phoenix connection as workable with the original rental-return buffer, and requested a concise materials-security and receipt checklist.

messages.content: Texas curveballs: the Dallas fair sent a new load-in map, Waco says hot breakfast starts too late for my Wednesday departure, and American nudged the Austin connection by a little bit. Can you sanity-check the final ground plan?

Yes. I would keep the Dallas garage plan rather than trying to improvise surface parking. The new map mainly changes how you enter and unload: aim for the marked garage entrance, keep the QR/parking confirmation handy, and arrive closer to 3:20 so you have time to get the boxes upstairs before the fair starts.
The map says SUVs should use the north entrance and no unloading at the curb. We have the garage reservation already. Should I change anything?

No change to the reservation. Add a note in the trip folder: north garage entrance, fair load-in level, no curb unload. Confirm the garage clearance one more time against the rental category, and print or screenshot the parking pass in case cell service is messy.
For Waco, I need to leave about 6:10 Wednesday. Their hot breakfast is now 7:00.

Treat the hotel breakfast as unavailable that morning. Best backup: buy coffee, yogurt, fruit, and a protein bar Tuesday night after the Waco fair, then use the room fridge. If the lobby has any grab-and-go items early, consider that a bonus, not the plan.
American moved the Phoenix connection to 66 minutes. Still okay?

Still workable, but I would not tighten the Austin airport timing. Keep the Round Rock departure conservative, return the SUV around 1:30, and go straight through security for the 3:05 flight. In Phoenix, skip a sit-down meal and stay near the next gate.
Can you give me the final short checklist for materials and receipts?

Trip-folder checklist: 1) Dallas garage pass, load-in map, and north-entrance note. 2) Keep boxes covered in the SUV; do not leave materials visible overnight. Bring the banner tube and any high-value packets into each hotel. 3) Recount boxes after each fair/school visit. 4) Waco breakfast backup bought Tuesday night. 5) Austin: fuel before return if required, rental return by 1:30, 66-minute Phoenix connection. 6) Save airfare receipt, hotel folios, rental receipt, one-way fee, fuel, tolls, Dallas parking, and any materials shipping or baggage receipts.

memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Tessa is planning a late-October Mesa volleyball weekend for three family members, can leave Salt Lake around 3:30 Friday, is weighing all-family travel versus one-parent travel, wants a two-queen room with breakfast and parking, and is wary of holding a team block without written cancellation terms.

verified_habit_signals.evidence_quote: We need one room with two queens

messages.content: Switching from admissions travel to family logistics: my younger one has a club volleyball tournament in Mesa the last weekend of October. Early Saturday pool play is possible, Sunday brackets could run into the afternoon, and the team hotel block has fuzzy cancellation terms. Can you compare flying versus driving for three of us?
I can. Two details affect the recommendation: which Mesa venue, and what is the earliest you can leave Salt Lake on Friday after school and work?

Arizona Athletic Grounds in east Mesa. Realistically we can leave our house at 3:30 Friday. If we drive, it would be after school too. First match time is not posted yet, but the coach warned us to plan for early.

With a 3:30 Friday start, flying is much kinder to Saturday. Driving is roughly 10.5 to 11.5 hours before longer stops, so you would be arriving very late or splitting the drive and losing Friday night anyway. A late-afternoon SLC-PHX flight gets you to a rental car and east Mesa hotel around dinner or shortly after.
What about just sending one parent with her? I am trying not to make this a giant production.

That is the lowest-cost flight version, but it has trade-offs: one parent handles the gear, meals, possible bracket changes, and any late-night return alone. For an early Saturday start, I would rank it: fly all three if fares are reasonable, fly one parent plus athlete if cost is the deciding factor, drive only if flights are unusually high or you can leave much earlier.
The team block says it is about 7 minutes from the venue, $179, but I do not see cancellation terms or breakfast. What other areas should I consider?

Shortlist the areas this way: East Mesa/Gateway area is closest to the venue and easiest for warmups, but dining can be more limited. Gilbert/SanTan Village adds about 15 to 20 minutes and gives better dinner choices. Mesa Riverview/Tempe is better for airport access and food, but it is too far for an early first serve.
We need one room with two queens, parking, and breakfast if possible. I do not want to be hunting for food before a 7 a.m. warmup.

Then I would hold a refundable two-queen backup near East Mesa or Gilbert with breakfast and free parking, even if it is a few minutes farther than the team block. The team hotel is only worth holding if they confirm: cancellable deadline, two queens guaranteed, breakfast status, parking cost, and no resort or event fee.
Can you put the family schedule impact in a quick table?

Plan | Friday impact | Saturday risk | Notes. Fly all three | Leave home about 3:30, catch late-afternoon/early-evening flight, hotel by evening | Low | Best rest, highest cost. Drive all three | Arrive around 2 a.m. or later with stops | High | Cheapest transport, worst for early play. One parent flies with athlete | Similar timing to flying all three | Low to medium | Cheaper, but more solo logistics.
Should I book the team block now while I wait on the game schedule?

Only if you can get the cancellation terms in writing today. Otherwise, hold the refundable backup first. For this weekend I would plan on flying Friday, staying two nights in a two-queen room near East Mesa or Gilbert, using the hotel breakfast as the morning plan, and choosing a Sunday return late enough to survive a bracket run. We can tighten flights once the first match and last possible final are posted.

memory_annotations.evidence_summary: After the Mesa schedule firmed up, Tessa chose flying over driving, selected the refundable two-queen hotel with breakfast and free parking over the nonrefundable team block, chose the later Sunday return to protect a possible late final, and decided to rent a car for tournament flexibility.

verified_habit_signals.evidence_quote: The refundable one is $164, cancelable until Thursday, breakfast starts at 6:00, two queens confirmed. The team block is $149, nonrefundable, and breakfast is not included.
two queens confirmed

messages.content: Mesa update: first match is 8:00 Saturday, and the latest Sunday final could start around 4:30 with awards after. The team block now only has nonrefundable rooms. A refundable hotel about 12 minutes farther has two queens, breakfast, and free parking. Help me choose.

Given the 8:00 Saturday start, I would fly rather than drive. I would also skip the nonrefundable team block. The refundable hotel costs a little more in drive time, but it protects you if the bracket shifts or anyone gets sick, and breakfast plus free parking offsets part of the rate difference.
The refundable one is $164, cancelable until Thursday, breakfast starts at 6:00, two queens confirmed. The team block is $149, nonrefundable, and breakfast is not included.

That makes the refundable hotel the better value. For $15 more before taxes, you get cancellation flexibility, confirmed bedding, breakfast, and parking. For Saturday, plan to be downstairs at 6:05, eat quickly or grab items to go, leave by about 6:35, and arrive with cushion for a 7:15ish warmup.
Flights are close. Friday options: 4:25, 5:15, or 6:05 out of Salt Lake. Sunday return options are 7:30 or 9:10. Monday morning is available but ugly for school and work.

I would avoid Monday. For Friday, the 5:15 is the safest balance if school pickup makes 4:25 rushed; the 6:05 is fine but pushes dinner and hotel arrival later. For Sunday, choose 9:10. A 7:30 return is too tight if a 4:30 final runs long, awards happen, and you still need to reach PHX, return the car, and clear security.
The 9:10 return costs about $45 more per person than the 7:30. Still worth it?

For this schedule, yes. The extra $135 buys a real buffer against missing the flight. Missing the 7:30 would likely cost more than that and turn into either a very late rebooking or Monday travel anyway.
Do we need a rental car if the hotel mentions a shuttle?

Yes, I would rent a car. Tournament shuttles are rarely flexible enough for warmups, food runs, and bracket changes. A midsize car should work unless you are carrying extra team gear; free hotel parking makes that easy.
Okay. Book the refundable hotel, Friday 5:15, Sunday 9:10, and a car. Give me the notes for the confirmation email to my spouse.

Confirmation notes: Fly SLC-PHX Friday on the 5:15 option after school/work; return Sunday on the 9:10 option to protect a possible late final and awards. Book the refundable two-queen hotel 12 minutes farther from the venue: $164, cancelable until Thursday, breakfast from 6:00, free parking. Skip the nonrefundable team block because it lacks breakfast and flexibility. Rent a midsize car for airport, venue, and food runs. Saturday plan: breakfast at 6:05, leave hotel 6:35, warmup buffer for the 8:00 match. Sunday: keep bags in the car, choose an easy early dinner near the venue or airport after brackets, and leave for PHX as soon as awards finish. Save flight, hotel, rental, parking, and any tournament-fee receipts.

memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Mesa pretrip plan was kept: fly Friday after school/work, guarantee late hotel arrival, keep the two-queen room with breakfast and free parking, use a 6:35 PM Sunday venue cutoff for the 9:10 PHX return, and try to improve scattered seats without changing flights.

messages.content: Quick Mesa check: the court assignments finally posted, and the hotel emailed asking me to guarantee our Friday late arrival. Can you sanity-check the timeline and the Sunday flight before I call them?

Yes. With the 5:15 SLC-PHX flight, you should land around early evening local time, then allow 25-35 minutes for bags and rental car pickup and roughly 35-40 minutes to East Mesa/Gilbert. I would tell the hotel you expect to arrive around 7:30-8:00 and ask them to guarantee the two-queen room. What is the latest possible Sunday final now?
Saturday first match is still 8:00. Sunday gold final can start as late as 4:30, and awards are listed as 20-30 minutes after. Also, our seats are scattered on the outbound.

Friday still works: breakfast at 6:00 Saturday, leave the hotel by 6:35, and you have room for parking and warmup. For seats, check the app now for any pair plus single; if not, ask at the gate and prioritize one parent next to your teen. Sunday is workable if awards finish by about 6:15. If the final starts late or goes long, the 9:10 return gets tight.
Give me a firm airport cutoff so I am not doing math from the bleachers.

Leave the venue by 6:35 at the latest. That gives you the drive to PHX, a fuel stop if needed, rental return, and a reasonable security buffer. Leaving at 6:45 is uncomfortable but maybe survivable; leaving at 7:00 is where I would expect stress.
Would you switch us to Monday morning just to be safe?

I would keep the 9:10 unless Monday morning is painless for school and work. Monday buys calm, but it adds another hotel night and makes everyone miss Monday. The current return is the right compromise as long as you treat 6:35 as the real gym departure time.
Okay, keep it. What exactly should I put in the hotel note?

Use this: Late arrival guaranteed by card; family arriving Friday around 7:30-8:00 PM after flight into PHX. Please hold the two-queen room and note late check-in. Please confirm free parking and breakfast starting at 6:00 AM. Also ask whether there is any issue parking after 8:00 PM and whether the room type is guaranteed, not just requested.

memory_annotations.evidence_summary: For the upper Midwest loop, Tessa prioritized Thursday arrival reliability and manageable winter driving over the lowest fare, accepted a one-way rental if justified, asked to compare Chicago and MSP backups, and planned around breakfast, parking, dinner access, and secure materials handling.

verified_habit_signals.evidence_quote: Delta is fine if the timing works, but I care more about not creating a terrible connection.

messages.content: Mesa is behind us, and now I have the draft Midwest route. It would be Sunday Nov. 10 through Thursday Nov. 14: Monday 8:00 counselor breakfast in St. Paul, Monday evening fair in Minneapolis, Tuesday school visits around Eau Claire and La Crosse, Wednesday evening transfer fair in Madison, and Thursday late-morning counselor meeting near Milwaukee. I need to tell my director which routing makes sense before I ask for approval.

Got it. Before I rank it, two practical questions: how much recruitment material are you moving, and do you need to be home Thursday night, or could Friday morning be acceptable if the route gets messy?

Two medium brochure boxes, table throw, and the banner. I can check one bag or ship a box. I really need to be home Thursday night if practical. I do not want to chase the cheapest option if it creates a bad Thursday.

Then I would rank the route shapes this way: 1) Fly into Minneapolis-St. Paul and home from Milwaukee: best fit for the actual path, but price the one-way rental fee. 2) Fly round trip MSP: possibly cheaper airfare and rental, but Thursday becomes a long backtrack from Milwaukee to MSP. 3) Fly into MSP and return from Chicago: useful backup if Milwaukee fares are unreasonable, but Chicago traffic and airport transfer time are real risks. 4) Drive the whole trip from Salt Lake City: best for materials control, worst for time, weather exposure, and fatigue.
I was worried the one-way car fee would make the open-jaw version look wasteful.

It may look higher on the rental line, but compare it against the cost of five extra hours Thursday, possible winter driving, fuel, parking, and the risk of missing a return. For approval, I would frame the open-jaw plan as buying schedule reliability, not convenience.
What about Chicago because Milwaukee is not that far from O'Hare?

Chicago is a reasonable backup for the return only. I would not start there because Chicago to St. Paul is too much deadhead driving. Returning from O'Hare or Midway after the Milwaukee meeting could work if flights are much better, but you would need to protect tolls, traffic, rental return, and weather. Milwaukee is cleaner if the fare is not outrageous.
Can you sketch the open-jaw route like I would actually drive it?

Sunday: fly SLC to MSP, pick up the rental, sleep St. Paul/Roseville. Monday: breakfast in St. Paul, keep the car parked or near the hotel midday, fair in Minneapolis that evening, then sleep St. Paul/Roseville or just east of the cities. Tuesday: drive to Eau Claire and La Crosse visits, then sleep La Crosse if the day runs late or Madison if the last visit ends early enough. Wednesday: Madison prep and evening transfer fair, sleep Madison. Thursday: drive to the suburban Milwaukee meeting, return the car at MKE, fly home after lunch.
Would you drive to Eau Claire after the Monday evening fair?

Not unless Tuesday's first appointment forces it. After an evening fair, load-out, and mid-November darkness, that drive is a fatigue risk. I would rather stay on the east side of the Twin Cities and leave early Tuesday with coffee and a clean weather check.
The materials in the rental car worry me a little.

Use a midsize SUV or crossover if reimbursement allows, keep the boxes low and covered, and do not leave the banner or high-value packets visible overnight. Better: ship one brochure box to the St. Paul breakfast site or first hotel, check one box or duffel, and carry the banner with you. Save shipping and baggage receipts either way.
What hotel areas should I look at before I send this?

For Sunday and Monday, look at St. Paul or Roseville first: easier breakfast/fair access, likely parking, and better odds of breakfast included. Woodbury or Hudson helps Tuesday morning but adds Monday evening logistics. For Tuesday/Wednesday, Madison east or near the fair is practical if parking is included and dinner is nearby. For Thursday, only use a Milwaukee-suburb hotel if you decide to move after the Madison fair or if the meeting host adds something Wednesday night.
What flights should I ask them to price? Delta is fine if the timing works, but I care more about not creating a terrible connection.

Ask for SLC to MSP Sunday afternoon or early evening, nonstop if available or one simple connection if not. For Thursday, ask for MKE to SLC after 2:00 PM with no more than one comfortable connection. Also ask them to price ORD or MDW as a backup return and MSP round trip as a comparison, but not as the recommended plan.
Can you give me the approval paragraph? I want to send it before I get pulled into visits.

Send this: Recommended routing is SLC-MSP on Sunday and MKE-SLC on Thursday with a one-way rental car. This follows the event path from St. Paul/Minneapolis to Eau Claire/La Crosse, Madison, and Milwaukee without requiring a Thursday backtrack. Please also price MSP round trip and a Chicago-area return as backups, but those add winter-driving and timing risk. I will look for hotels with breakfast, parking, and nearby dinner options, and I will either ship one materials box ahead or check materials so boxes are not left exposed in the vehicle.

memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Tessa chose the open-jaw MSP inbound/MKE outbound as the most reliable route, leaned toward St. Paul over Roseville when the small price difference bought easier Monday logistics, kept Madison for the late Wednesday fair, and treated Milwaukee as an optional weather backup rather than the main overnight.

messages.content: Midwest update before I book holds: La Crosse moved earlier Tuesday, Madison confirmed the transfer fair runs until 9:15 Wednesday, and the Milwaukee meeting stayed Thursday at 10:45 in Wauwatosa. Hotels by the Minneapolis fair are above cap or charge for parking. St. Paul and Roseville have breakfast and free parking. Air desk found a Thursday MKE option at 2:20 with one MSP connection; MSP round trip is cheaper but means driving back after Milwaukee.

I would rank them: 1) MSP inbound and MKE outbound, still the best match. 2) Chicago-area return only if MKE jumps dramatically in price. 3) MSP round trip, acceptable only as a budget fallback. The 2:20 MKE return after a 10:45 Wauwatosa meeting is much calmer than finishing the meeting and then driving back toward Minneapolis.
For Sunday night, is St. Paul worth about $18 more than Roseville?

If the breakfast is in St. Paul and the St. Paul hotel also includes parking and breakfast, yes, the $18 is defensible. Roseville is fine if the room is cleaner or cancellation terms are better, but it adds a morning drive and another chance for traffic before the 8:00 breakfast.
Does the earlier La Crosse visit make Roseville too far for Monday night?

It makes the start early but not impossible. If you keep the St. Paul/Roseville base Monday night, choose the east/southeast side of that area, pack the car after the fair, and plan a very early departure. I would avoid anything west of Minneapolis. If the La Crosse visit is before 10:00 and weather looks bad, consider a refundable midpoint backup, but I would not add that unless the forecast forces it.
I can tolerate the early start. I do not want to add another town unless we have to.

Then the clean overnight sequence is: Sunday St. Paul, Monday St. Paul or Roseville on the east side, Tuesday Madison after the La Crosse/Eau Claire visits, Wednesday Madison again after the late transfer fair, then Thursday morning Madison to Wauwatosa and MKE after the meeting.
What about sleeping near Milwaukee Wednesday so Thursday morning is easier?

That helps Thursday but creates the worse drive at the worse time. Leaving Madison after a 9:15 fair means load-out, dinner or no dinner, then 75-90 minutes in the dark. Staying in Madison gives you a normal checkout and a controlled Thursday drive. I would only hold Milwaukee as a weather backup if it cancels late enough.
The MKE flight is 2:20 to MSP, 88-minute connection, then into SLC around 6:45. The MSP round trip has a 5:05 nonstop home.

Take the MKE option if approval allows it. The 88-minute connection is reasonable, and the airport is close enough after Wauwatosa. The 5:05 MSP nonstop looks nice on paper, but it depends on a long post-meeting drive with no weather or traffic problem. That is the weaker reliability choice.
Which refundable rooms should I hold today?

Hold these first: 1) St. Paul Sunday night, breakfast included, free parking, close to the Monday breakfast. 2) Roseville Monday night only if St. Paul is over cap or the cancellation terms are better; otherwise keep St. Paul both nights to simplify. 3) Madison Tuesday and Wednesday nights, preferably near the fair or on the east side with parking and a restaurant nearby. 4) Optional Milwaukee-area Wednesday backup only if it has same-day or late-Tuesday cancellation. Cancel any backup once the forecast and final host addresses are firm.

memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Tessa finalized the upper Midwest open-jaw trip, chose the Delta return with a safer Detroit connection over cheaper or tighter options, requested window seats, reserved a midsize SUV for materials, and booked refundable queen-bed hotel rooms with breakfast, parking, and dinner access noted.

messages.content: Approval came through for the open-jaw plan. Can we move this from holds into actual reservations? I need SLC to Minneapolis on Sunday Nov. 10 after about 1 PM, then Milwaukee to SLC Thursday Nov. 14 after the 10:45 meeting. One connection is fine if it is not stressful. Also please request window seats where you can, reserve a car with room for materials boxes, and lock the three hotels with queen beds, breakfast, parking details, and dinner nearby.

Yes. The one piece I want you to choose is the Thursday return because it affects connection comfort. Outbound is easy: Delta nonstop SLC-MSP, 2:20 PM to 5:58 PM, $281. Return choices: Delta via Detroit, 3:05 PM to 7:40 PM, 1h42 connection, $386; United via Denver, 2:15 PM to 6:25 PM, 1h10 connection, $319; Delta via Minneapolis, 12:25 PM to 4:45 PM, 42-minute connection, $332. I would skip the 42-minute one. Do you want the cheaper United routing or the Delta routing with the bigger cushion?
Do the Delta via Detroit. The extra cost is easier to justify than sprinting through a connection.

Flight is set as Delta SLC-MSP Sunday 2:20-5:58 nonstop, then MKE-DTW-SLC Thursday 3:05-7:40 with 1h42 in Detroit. Window seats selected or requested where the map allowed: 14A outbound, 18F MKE-DTW, and 21A DTW-SLC. Fare total is $667. For the car, the midsize SUV is $347 plus taxes, pickup MSP Sunday around 6:30 PM and drop MKE Thursday about 1:15 PM. A standard car is about $60 less but tight for boxes.
Reserve the SUV. What hotel set came out best? I would rather keep St. Paul both Sunday and Monday if it is not over cap.

Best practical set: St. Paul Sunday-Monday, Hampton Inn & Suites Downtown, $151/night, two-queen refundable room, breakfast from 6:00, parking $15/night, several dinner spots within a few blocks. Madison Tuesday, Hampton Madison East Towne, $139, queen room, breakfast from 6:00, free parking, chain restaurants and a grocery close by. Brookfield Wednesday, Fairfield Inn & Suites Milwaukee Brookfield, $156, two queens, breakfast from 6:30, free parking, restaurants along Bluemound Road. All three show queen bedding rather than double-only rooms.
Book those refundable. One queen is fine when available; two queens is fine if that is the refundable option. Please add a late-arrival note for Sunday.

Reserved. St. Paul confirmation ends 4821, Madison 7736, Brookfield 9154. Notes added: late arrival Sunday after MSP flight, please hold confirmed queen-bed room type, traveler arriving with admissions materials. Breakfast hours and parking were confirmed from the hotel listings today; I would still glance at the front desk signs on arrival in case of holiday-week staffing changes. Cancellation windows are Saturday for St. Paul, Monday evening for Madison, and Tuesday evening for Brookfield.
Can you give me the reimbursement note, especially for the higher airfare and one-way car?

Use this: Recommended routing is SLC-MSP outbound and MKE-SLC return because the recruitment path moves east across Minnesota and Wisconsin and ends in the Milwaukee area. Although the open-jaw airfare and one-way SUV rental are modestly higher than a Minneapolis round trip, they avoid a Thursday backtrack of several hours, reduce winter-driving risk, and keep the traveler available for the 10:45 Milwaukee meeting. The midsize SUV is needed to transport admissions materials securely between school visits and fairs.
Great. Anything else before I put the receipts into Concur?

Upload the flight receipt, rental estimate, and all three hotel confirmations. Add the St. Paul parking line separately so it does not look like an unexplained rate increase. For materials, keep the box label list on your phone, bring the folio bag inside each night, and leave nothing visible in the car. I also added reminders for hotel cancellation deadlines, flight check-in, and a Thursday airport departure target of 12:45 PM from the Milwaukee stop.

memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Tessa chose a later return with a more comfortable connection, accepted the later arrival for reliability, switched the Madison breakfast plan to grab-and-go, added winter-driving buffers, and tightened receipt and materials-security logistics.

verified_habit_signals.evidence_quote: The Detroit connection is now 39 minutes, which feels too tight.
Move me to the later Delta.

messages.content: Delta just changed my Milwaukee return. The Detroit connection is now 39 minutes, which feels too tight. Also the forecast for Tuesday and Wednesday looks like early winter slush, the Madison hotel says breakfast will start at 6:30 instead of 6, and Milwaukee sent a separate materials drop-off gate for Thursday. Can you help me clean this up?

I would not keep the 39-minute Detroit connection unless arriving early is more important than reliability. Options now: keep it and land around 7:30 if everything works; move to Delta via MSP, 4:20 PM to 9:35 PM with a 1h18 connection, about $42 more or possibly covered by the schedule-change waiver; or switch to United via Denver, 2:55 PM to 7:10 PM with only 55 minutes. My vote is the later Delta via MSP if getting home around 10:15 is acceptable.
Move me to the later Delta. Late is better than sprinting or missing it.

Changed to MKE-MSP-SLC, departing 4:20 PM and arriving SLC 9:35 PM. Window seats were reselected/requested on both legs. I moved the rental return target to 2:45 PM, which gives you time for the Thursday drop-off gate, receipt check, and security. Build in 30 extra minutes Tuesday from St. Paul toward western Wisconsin and 45 extra minutes Wednesday into Madison if slush actually develops.
For Madison, I have a 7:15 visit in Sun Prairie and need to leave by 6:20. What is the breakfast plan?

Do not rely on the hotel breakfast that morning. On Tuesday night, grab yogurt, fruit, and a protein bar from the nearby grocery or Kwik Trip and keep it in the room fridge. Use lobby coffee if it is out early; otherwise get coffee after the school visit. Panera opening at 6 is too tight with weather.
Can you give me a tight packing and receipt checklist? I leave Sunday.

Checklist: printed schedule plus host phone numbers; Delta change email and new boarding passes; rental agreement and fuel receipt; hotel folios with parking separated; campus parking or gate instructions for Milwaukee; materials inventory photo before pickup and before return; one snow brush or scraper from home; boots or shoes that can handle slush; phone charger in the car; all receipts photographed nightly. Do not leave counselor cards, scanner, or folio bag in the SUV overnight.

memory_annotations.evidence_summary: For Thanksgiving, Tessa chose all four flying on Southwest under the airfare ceiling despite open seating, selected a Sunday afternoon return to protect Monday, and held a Kearny Mesa two-queen hotel with breakfast, free parking, and nearby food.

easy food would help.

messages.content: The recruiting trip is finally wrapped, so now I need to face Thanksgiving. My spouse's family confirmed San Diego. We can leave after early school release Wednesday Nov. 27 and need to be back Sunday Dec. 1 at a sane hour for Monday school and work. Four of us. Relatives have very limited sleeping space, so probably a hotel. Can you compare flying versus driving?

I can. For that holiday window, flying will protect Monday better, but driving may be much cheaper if fares have jumped. I need the relatives' neighborhood and the earliest realistic airport departure. Also, should I assume all four travel together, or do you want me to price a split plan with only part of the family going?
All four if we can make it work. They are near Clairemont Mesa Boulevard and I-5. We could leave the house around 1 PM Wednesday. If airfare is awful, driving is still on the table.

Here is the practical comparison. Fly all four: Southwest nonstop SLC-SAN 5:20-6:25 Wednesday and SAN-SLC 3:05-5:55 Sunday, about $408 per person or $1,632 total; Delta nonstop 3:45-4:50 Wednesday and 6:15-9:10 Sunday, about $462 per person or $1,848 total; cheapest late combo is about $1,504 total but lands close to midnight Sunday. Drive: about 750 miles each way, 11-12 hours without much margin; direct Wednesday after school gets you in very late, and splitting through Las Vegas adds motel cost and cuts into Thanksgiving morning. Hotel areas: Kearny Mesa/Clairemont is closest, Mission Valley has more food, Old Town is workable but parking is often pricier.
If we can keep airfare under about $1,700, I would rather fly. The Southwest timing looks best. For the hotel, two queens, breakfast, parking, and easy food would help.

One trade-off: Southwest saves money and includes bags, but seats are not assigned. For four people on a holiday flight, I would set check-in alarms or add EarlyBird if the price is reasonable. Delta costs about $216 more total on the current fares and lets you choose seats now. Is the savings worth the open seating for this trip?
For this one, yes. The teenagers can handle not sitting right next to us. Let's do Southwest and set check-in alarms.

Then I would hold the Hampton Inn San Diego-Kearny Mesa. It is closest to the Clairemont/I-5 area, about $189/night refundable, two-queen room available, breakfast starts at 6:00, free parking, and there are casual restaurants on Convoy and Clairemont Mesa nearby. Backups: Holiday Inn Express Mission Bay at about $204 with breakfast but some parking uncertainty, or Homewood Suites Mission Valley around $229 with more space but higher parking and a longer drive to relatives.
Hold the Hampton. Relatives can pick us up Wednesday, but not Sunday, so rideshare back to the airport is fine. Please make sure the Sunday return does not wreck Monday.

Held: Southwest outbound Wednesday 5:20 PM SLC to 6:25 PM SAN, return Sunday 3:05 PM SAN to 5:55 PM SLC. That return is the best balance I found because it avoids the late-night holiday crowd and gets everyone home before dinner. Hampton Kearny Mesa is held Wednesday through Sunday in a two-queen refundable room. Add a rideshare budget of about $35-$50 for the Sunday hotel-to-airport trip depending traffic.
